utterances.message: [I need to phrase this carefully.] Not about the chapter, no. I've got a query about your course aims.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [She's avoiding the issue. I need to be direct.] Well, I don't. There's nothing written up there about using defensive spells.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Oh, Harry. This is more complicated than he realizes.] (grimly) The thing is, Harry, I'm not sure they did. Oh, let's get out of here.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to explain this carefully.] Look, you don't understand what it was like after it happened. You arrived back in the middle of the lawn clutching Cedric's dead body... None of us saw what happened in the maze... We just had Dumbledore's word for it that You-Know-Who had come back and killed Cedric and fought you.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to calm him down. He's misunderstanding me.] I know it is, Harry, so will you please stop biting my head off? It's just that before the truth could sink in, everyone went home for the summer, where they spent two months reading about how you're a nutcase and Dumbledore's going senile!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [He's taking this so hard. We need to be there for him.] No, Harry. Some people believe you. It's just... it's easier for them not to, you know? Accepting that You-Know-Who is back is terrifying.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [We can't let Malfoy see us worried.] Dumbledore would know if something had happened to Hagrid. It's just playing into Malfoy's hands to look worried, it tells him we don't know exactly what's going on. We've got to ignore him, Harry.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to keep Harry from doing something rash.] Harry, don't go picking a row with Malfoy, don't forget, he's a prefect now, he could make life difficult for you...

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Oh, Harry's back. I hope his detention wasn't too bad.] (Jerking awake) Oh, Harry, it's you... Good about Ron, isn't it? (Yawning) I'm just so — so — so tired.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [This sounds serious. Could Umbridge be working with Voldemort?] (Listening intently) You're worried that You-Know-Who's controlling her like he controlled Quirrell?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [We need to consider all possibilities.] I suppose so. But I don't think he can be possessing her the way he possessed Quirrell... Harry, I think you ought to tell Dumbledore your scar hurt.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Why is he being so stubborn?] Harry, I'm sure Dumbledore would want to be bothered by this —

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [This is unexpected.] (Sounding surprised) Blimey, it is! What's Percy writing to you for?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [We should find out what it says.] (Eagerly) Open it!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'm worried about how this is affecting both Harry and Ron.] (Looking at Ron with an odd expression) Oh, give them here.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [They need help, and this might distract them from Percy's letter.] Give them to me, I'll look through them and correct them.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [They need to learn from this.] (Holding out her hands) What you can say is, 'We promise we'll never leave our homework this late again.'

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'm outraged by this discrimination.] What's she got against werewolves?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to share this important information with Harry and Ron.] (Reading aloud from the newspaper) "In a surprise move last night the Ministry of Magic passed new legislation giving itself an unprecedented level of control at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'm getting increasingly angry as I read.] (Continuing to read) "'The Minister has been growing uneasy about goings-on at Hogwarts for some time,' said Junior Assistant to the Minister, Percy Weasley."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'm outraged by this development.] (Finishing the article) It's outrageous. It's... (Breathing fast, eyes bright) I can't believe this.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'm worried about being late to class.] (Jumping up) Well, come on, we'd better get going, if she's inspecting Binns's class we don't want to be late...

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to approach this carefully.] (Speaking suddenly) "I was wondering whether you'd thought any more about Defense Against the Dark Arts, Harry."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to be more direct.] "I meant the idea Ron and I had — oh, all right, the idea I had, then — about you teaching us."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [He's considering it! I need to encourage him.] (Eagerly) "And?"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to boost his confidence.] (Gently) "Yes, Harry. But all the same, there's no point pretending that you're not good at Defense Against the Dark Arts, because you are. You were the only person last year who could throw off the Imperius Curse completely, you can produce a Patronus, you can do all sorts of stuff that full-grown wizards can't. Viktor always said —"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Oh, Ron, not now.] (In a bored voice) "Ho ho. He said Harry knew how to do stuff even he didn't, and he was in the final year at Durmstrang."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [This is not the time for Ron's jealousy.] (Coolly, with a slightly pink face) "So what if I am? I can have a pen pal if I —"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to refocus on Harry.] (Turning back to Harry) "Well, what do you think? Will you teach us?"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to explain the broader plan.] (Looking anxious) "Well, now, don't fly off the handle again, Harry, please. But I really think you ought to teach anyone who wants to learn. I mean, we're talking about defending ourselves against V-Voldemort — oh, don't be pathetic, Ron — it doesn't seem fair if we don't offer the chance to other people."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to reassure him and propose a plan.] (Leaning forward) "Well, I think you might be surprised how many people would be interested in hearing what you've got to say. Look, you know the first weekend in October's a Hogsmeade weekend? How would it be if we tell anyone who's interested to meet us in the village and we can talk it over?"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to explain the risks.] (Returning to her work) "Because I don't think Umbridge would be very happy if she found out what we were up to."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to start this meeting confidently.] (Speaking in a slightly high-pitched voice) "Er, well, er - hi. Well... erm... well, you know why you're here. Erm... well, Harry here had the idea - I mean" (glancing at Harry's sharp look) "I had the idea - that it might be good if people who wanted to study Defense Against the Dark Arts - and I mean, really study it, you know, not the rubbish that Umbridge is doing with us - because nobody could call that Defense Against the Dark Arts -"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [That's encouraging.] (Speaking more confidently) "Well, I thought it would be good if we, well, took matters into our own hands. And by that I mean learning how to defend ourselves properly, not just theory but the real spells -"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to emphasize the bigger picture.] "Of course I do. But I want more than that, I want to be properly trained in Defense because... because..." (Taking a deep breath) "Because Lord Voldemort's back."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to diffuse this situation.] "Well, Dumbledore believes it -"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to get this meeting back on track.] (Speaking in a high-pitched voice) "So... like I was saying... if you want to learn some defense, then we need to work out how we're going to do it, how often we're going to meet, and where we're going to -"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to reassure them.] (Speaking in a low voice) "No, they can't have done because I put a jinx on that piece of parchment we all signed. Believe me, if anyone's run off and told Umbridge, we'll know exactly who they are and they will really regret it."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I hope this deters any potential traitors.] (Speaking grimly) "Well, put it this way, it'll make Eloise Midgen's acne look like a couple of cute freckles."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to explain my theory carefully.] Umbridge has been reading your mail, Harry. There's no other explanation. (She speaks in a hushed tone while practicing her charm)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'm almost certain of my deduction.] I'm almost certain of it. (She notices Harry's distraction) Watch your frog, it's escaping.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I should explain my reasoning.] I've been suspecting this ever since Filch accused you of ordering Dungbombs, because it seemed such a stupid lie. (She continues explaining her theory in whispers)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I should help Ron with the charm while continuing our discussion.] It's the way you're moving your wand. You don't want to wave it, it's more a sharp jab.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'll demonstrate to help Ron.] Fine, let's swap. (She seizes Ron's raven and replaces it with her frog)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I can't shake off my doubts about our plans.] Just thinking . . . (She continues to stare out the window, lost in thought)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to voice my concerns carefully.] No . . . not exactly . . . More . . . wondering . . . I suppose we're doing the right thing . . . I think . . . aren't we?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to be more direct.] I was just wondering whether we're doing the right thing, starting this Defense Against the Dark Arts group.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I know I'm contradicting myself, but I have to express my concerns.] I know. But after talking to Snuffles . . . (She twists her fingers together nervously)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [This sounds too good to be true.] Harry, are you sure about this? Dobby's plans aren't always safe. Remember when he made you lose all the bones in your arm?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [If Dumbledore knows about it, it must be safe.] Oh well, that's all right then. (She looks relieved)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [We need to be organized about this.] I'll start spreading the word discreetly. We should use the coin system we discussed to communicate the time and place.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Ron looks awful. I hope this helps.] (Kisses Ron on the cheek) Good luck, Ron. And you, Harry—

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [They're both so miserable. I need to do something.] (stands up and walks to the window, watching the snow) Well, I can think of one thing that might cheer you both up.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [This will definitely lift their spirits.] (turns back with a broad smile) Yeah. Hagrid's back.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [This is fascinating, but it sounds incredibly dangerous.] How could you tell which one was the Gurg?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [This is horrifying!] (gasping) Whose head?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I know this one!] (raises her hand) The only people who can see thestrals are people who have seen death.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [We need to approach this carefully.] Harry, how're you feeling?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [He's clearly not fine.] Oh, don't lie, Harry. (impatiently) Ron and Ginny say you've been hiding from everyone since you got back from St. Mungo's.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [We need to address the real issue.] Look, the others have told me what you overheard last night on the Extendable Ears—

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to reinforce this with logic.] Harry, you've had these dreams before. You had flashes of what Voldemort was up to last year.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [He needs facts to dispel these fears.] (exasperated) One day, you'll read Hogwarts, A History, and perhaps that will remind you that you can't Apparate or Disapparate inside Hogwarts. Even Voldemort couldn't just make you fly out of your dormitory, Harry.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'm still in shock. I can't believe we never knew about this.] (Tearfully) I never knew...

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I can't believe someone could be so cruel.] (Horrified) Bellatrix Lestrange did that? That woman Kreacher's got a photo of in his den?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [This is shocking! I need to tell Harry and Ron immediately.] (Lets out a yelp) Oh no!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [They need to see this for themselves.] (Spreads the newspaper on the table) Look at this!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [This is even worse than I thought.] They're Death Eaters, Harry. Look at the captions. Antonin Dolohov, convicted of murdering Gideon and Fabian Prewett...

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [We need to be prepared for what this means.] This is serious. If these Death Eaters have escaped, it means Voldemort is gaining power and influence.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [The Ministry's denial is frustrating but not surprising.] What other options does he have? He can hardly say, 'Sorry everyone, Dumbledore warned me this might happen, the Azkaban guards have joined Lord Voldemort' — stop whimpering, Ron — 'and now Voldemort's worst supporters have broken out too.'

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [People are in denial. It's easier than facing the truth.] Most students don't get the Daily Prophet, Harry. They probably don't know yet.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [We need to be prepared for anything.] We should be extra careful now. And maybe we should step up our efforts in the D.A.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [This is perfect! The interview is having exactly the effect we hoped for.] Harry! I think I know what this means — open this one first!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [We need to focus on the positive responses.] (excitedly) Here's another one you've convinced, Harry! 'Having read your side of the story I am forced to the conclusion that the Daily Prophet has treated you very unfairly...'

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I can't believe her audacity.] Oh, I expect she really fancied herself sitting up there in the Head's office.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [She makes me so angry.] (viciously) Lording it over all the other teachers, the stupid puffed-up, power-crazy old —

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Of course Umbridge would do something like this.] (angrily) Another one of Umbridge's little ideas, I suppose. Giving extra power to her favorite students.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to understand what's going on with Harry.] But why haven't you got Occlumency lessons anymore?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [He's clearly not telling us everything.] So you've stopped having funny dreams?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [This is serious. Harry needs to continue his lessons.] Well, I don't think Snape should stop until you're absolutely sure you can control them! Harry, I think you should go back to him and ask —

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [They need to take these exams seriously.] (Tapping Ron's schedule with her wand) If you follow that you should do fine.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [He should know this.] That's for Quidditch practice.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Harry seems distracted again.] What's wrong, Harry?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Maybe it's about Cho.] I saw Cho earlier, and she looked really miserable too... Have you two had a row again?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I hope they can work things out.] What about?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'm concerned for Ron but also skeptical.] But—

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I want to reassure Ron but also be realistic.] Well, if she does say that it'll be very unfair, you couldn't have done anything! But I'm sure she won't, I mean, if it's really true they've got premises in Diagon Alley now, they must have been planning this for ages...

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I share Ron's concern but have my own theories.] Well, yes, that occurred to me too. I've been wondering whether Mundungus has persuaded them to sell stolen goods or something awful...

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'm shocked and concerned.] (drops her teacup) Oh, Harry, you didn't!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'm surprised and concerned.] But you've lasted this long — What makes you think —

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'm terrified as I realize what we're looking at.] Hagrid, who is he?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'm on the verge of tears, overwhelmed by the situation.] But why? Why — what — oh, Hagrid!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I'm horrified and incredulous.] Harmless! He's been hurting you all this time, hasn't he? That's why you've had all these injuries!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [We have to tell him the truth. This is getting ridiculous.] (sighs heavily) Well, actually... no, Ron. As a matter of fact, the only bit of the match Harry and I saw was Davies's first goal.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I feel terrible. We need to explain.] Well — no. (reaches out placatingly) But Ron, we didn't want to leave — we had to!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [We need to make Ron understand the gravity of the situation.] (firmly) Well, he has. Grawp's about sixteen feet tall, enjoys ripping up twenty-foot pine trees, and knows me, (snorts) as Hermy.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I hate to admit it, but Ron's right.] (irritably, turning a page of her book) Yes. Yes, I'm starting to think he has. But unfortunately, he made Harry and me promise.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I know Ron's right, but I feel so guilty.] (in a small voice) I know, it's just that — we promised.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [I need to make sure I covered everything.] Well, it wasn't too bad, was it? I'm not sure I did myself justice on Cheering Charms, I just ran out of time. Did you put in the countercharm for hiccups? I wasn't sure whether I ought to, it felt like too much. And on question twenty-three—

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [They don't understand how important this is!] (looks frustrated but doesn't continue her analysis)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [We can't waste time relaxing!] (looks alarmed) A break? We need to start revising for Transfiguration! It's one of the most difficult subjects.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [At least Harry's being somewhat sensible.] (sighs) Fine, but only a short break. We can't afford to fall behind.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Concerned and skeptical] "But — but where? How?"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Trying to reason] "But Harry, think about this. It's five o'clock in the afternoon. . . . The Ministry of Magic must be full of workers. . . . How would Voldemort and Sirius have got in without being seen?"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Gently] "You've never been there, Harry. You've dreamed about the place, that's all."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Desperately] "Harry, I'm begging you, please! Please let's just check that Sirius isn't at home before we go charging off to London — if we find out he's not there then I swear I won't try and stop you, I'll come, I'll d-do whatever it takes to try and save him —"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Panicking as Umbridge threatens to use the Cruciatus Curse] "No! Professor Umbridge — it's illegal —"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Pretending to break down] "No — Harry — Harry, we'll have to tell her!"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Convincingly acting distraught] "We'll have to, Harry, she'll force it out of you anyway, what's... what's the point...?"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Feigning reluctance] "I'm — I'm sorry everyone. But — I can't stand it —"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Gulping] "Well, he was trying to speak to Professor Dumbledore..."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Scathingly, maintaining her act] "Of course not. Hagrid might have set it off accidentally."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Pointing into the dark trees] "In there, of course. It had to be somewhere that students weren't going to find it accidentally, didn't it?"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Confidently] "Oh yes. Yes, it's well hidden."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [In a steely voice] "Oh yes." (She crashes through the undergrowth loudly)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Sounding shaken but determined] "We need to get back up to the castle."

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Hopelessly] "Well, we can't do anything without wands. Anyway, Harry, how exactly were you planning to get all the way to London?"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Urgently] "Don't go calling for him, though!"

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
utterances.message: [Oh, Mr. Weasley...] Telephone. (whispers the correction)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [Oh, there he is!] (waves alongside Ron) Harry! Over here!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [I need to address this seriously.] (in a very serious voice) Did you really blow up your aunt, Harry?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [Boys can be so immature sometimes.] (sharply) It's not funny, Ron. Honestly, I'm amazed Harry wasn't expelled.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [He looks so pale. This is serious.] (Kneeling beside Harry) Are you okay, Harry? You sort of went rigid and fell out of your seat.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [I've read about dementors, but I never imagined they'd be so terrible.] (Watching Harry anxiously) Are you sure you're okay, Harry?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [There must be a logical explanation for this.] Harry, dementors are known to affect people differently. It doesn't mean you're weak.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [This is getting out of hand. I need to bring some rationality to this conversation.] (Speaking in a calm, logical tone) Probably a stray. (Pours herself some pumpkin juice) Coincidence.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [I need to make them see how ridiculous this is.] (In a superior tone) There you are, then. They see the Grim and die of fright. The Grim's not an omen, it's the cause of death! And Harry's still with us because he's not stupid enough to see one and think, right, well, I'd better kick the bucket then!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [Ron's being ridiculous. I need to point out his inconsistency.] You didn't seem quite so confident when you were telling Harry it was a sheep. (Opens her Arithmancy book) Professor Trelawney said you didn't have the right aura! You just don't like being bad at something for a change!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [We need to reassure him quickly!] (Gasps) You haven't been fired, Hagrid!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [We need to make Hagrid see this isn't his fault.] (Speaking earnestly) It's all Malfoy's fault, Hagrid!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [Hagrid needs to sober up if we're going to help him.] (Speaking firmly) I think you've had enough to drink, Hagrid. (Takes the tankard and goes outside to empty it)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [Finally, a chance to apply what we've learned!] (sits up straighter, looking eager)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [Oh, I know this!] (raises hand quickly) It's a shape-shifter. It can take the shape of whatever it thinks will frighten us most.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [I'm really anxious about this situation.] (whispers anxiously) Dumbledore obviously thinks he might be.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [That's a good point. I hadn't thought of that.] (nods in agreement)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [That's a terrifying thought.] (shudders)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [I can't believe no one else has read 'Hogwarts: A History'.] (sighs exasperatedly) Honestly, am I the only person who's ever bothered to read 'Hogwarts: A History'?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [I'll explain it to them, even though they should know this already.] Because the castle's protected by more than walls, you know. There are all sorts of enchantments on it, to stop people entering by stealth. You can't just Apparate in here. And I'd like to see the disguise that could fool those dementors. They're guarding every single entrance to the grounds. They'd have seen him fly in too. And Filch knows all the secret passages, they'll have them covered...

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [This must be about Buckbeak. I need to find out what's going on.] Hagrid, please calm down. Tell us what's happened. (speaking gently)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [We need to reassure Hagrid and start planning a defense.] Hagrid, listen. We'll help you prepare a defense for Buckbeak. I'm sure we can prove he's safe.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [There must be precedents we can use.] I'm sure I've read about a case of hippogriff-baiting where the hippogriff got off. I'll look it up for you, Hagrid.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [This is horrifying. How could they put an innocent person through that?] (shocked) But you were innocent! Surely that should have mattered!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [I should be studying, but Harry needs support right now.] (Puts down her book and leans forward) You're going to be fine, Harry. You've practiced so hard, and you've got a Firebolt!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [Oliver's intensity isn't helping. Harry needs to relax.] (Frowns at Wood) I think Harry needs to rest now, Oliver. He knows the plan.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [Boys and their Quidditch! But I suppose it's good to see Harry smiling a bit.] (Shakes her head but smiles) You two are impossible. Harry, why don't you try to get some sleep? You'll need all your energy tomorrow.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [I hope he can sleep. Maybe I should look up some calming charms, just in case.] Good night, Harry. And remember, no matter what happens tomorrow, we're proud of you.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [My mind is racing, trying to piece together this puzzle.] Professor Lupin, what's going on? How can you trust him?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [I need to approach this logically. There must be a rational explanation.] But Professor Lupin... Scabbers can't be Pettigrew... it just can't be true, you know it can't...

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [I've researched this thoroughly. I know I'm right about this.] Because... because people would know if Peter Pettigrew had been an Animagus. We did Animagi in class with Professor McGonagall. And I looked them up when I did my homework — the Ministry of Magic keeps tabs on witches and wizards who can become animals; there's a register showing what animal they become, and their markings and things... and I went and looked Professor McGonagall up on the register, and there have been only seven Animagi this century, and Pettigrew's name wasn't on the list —

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [I need to make sure Harry understands the gravity of our situation.] Harry, we've got to keep out of sight. We mustn't be seen. (Whispers urgently)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [He's right, but we need to be cautious.] You're right. (Nods slowly) But we've got to be careful. We mustn't be seen.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [We need to time this perfectly.] We have to wait until the Committee members have seen he's tied up. If we free him now, Hagrid will get in trouble for setting him loose.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [We can do this if we're careful.] It'll be enough. We just need to be quick and quiet.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [I remember this!] That's Hagrid breaking the milk jug. I'm going to find Scabbers in a moment...

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [We absolutely cannot do that!] No! (Whispers fiercely) Don't you understand? We're breaking one of the most important wizarding laws! Nobody's supposed to change time, nobody!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [We need to open this window quickly.] Stand back! (Takes out her wand) Alohomora!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (Harry Potter, #3)
utterances.message: [We can't waste another second!] GO!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Flying seems so imprecise. There must be some theory behind it.] (looking up from her book) I've been reading 'Quidditch Through the Ages', and it says that the most important thing is to keep a firm grip on your broom and lean slightly forward when you want to go higher.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [They don't understand the importance of preparation.] (huffily) Well, I think it's better to be prepared. What if something goes wrong?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I can't believe we're in this situation.] (gasping) I — told — you. I — told — you.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I know a spell for this!] (snarls) Oh, move over. (grabs Harry's wand) Alohomora!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I should remind him about his studies.] Just remember to keep up with your homework, Harry. You've been at Quidditch practice almost every evening.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Boys and their Quidditch.] (rolls her eyes) It's hardly a secret anymore, though. Everyone seems to know you're playing Seeker now, Harry.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I should help him prepare more.] Have you finished reading Quidditch Through the Ages, Harry? It might help you feel more prepared.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Boys and their Quidditch obsession.] (sighs) Let's hope none. The important thing is for Harry to play safely and follow the rules.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [This must be dark magic. We need to find out who's doing it.] (frantically) Can't be... Can't nothing interfere with a broomstick except powerful Dark magic...

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I need to look for the source.] (snatching the binoculars) Give them here! (scanning the crowd) I knew it! Snape — look.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [We need to stop him before Harry gets hurt.] He's doing something — jinxing the broom. We've got to do something!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I have an idea, but it's risky.] Leave it to me. (stands up) I'll be right back.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [This could be dangerous for Harry. We need a safe solution.] Pretend to break your leg.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Poor Neville! I need to help him.] (leaps up and performs the countercurse) What happened, Neville?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Finally, a breakthrough!] (excited) Stay there! (runs to get a book)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [This is it! The answer we've been looking for!] (returns with a large book) Nicolas Flamel is the only known maker of the Sorcerer's Stone!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [We need to approach this logically and carefully.] We shouldn't jump to conclusions. We don't have proof that Snape is actually trying to steal the Stone. (She leans forward, lowering her voice) But we should keep a close eye on him, just in case.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Ron's suggestion is tempting, but risky.] We can't do that, Ron. We don't have any real evidence. Plus, we're not supposed to know about the Stone in the first place. We'd get in trouble for snooping around.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [We need to be strategic about this.] We'll have to be very careful. Maybe we can ask Hagrid some subtle questions. He seems to know a lot about what's going on at Hogwarts.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [We need to flatter him a bit to get more information.] Oh, come on, Hagrid, you might not want to tell us, but you do know, you know everything that goes on round here.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Hagrid's definitely hiding something, but we need to focus on the Stone.] (Persistence in her voice) Hagrid, we're just curious about the Stone's protection. Surely you can tell us something? We know Dumbledore trusts you.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [We need to appeal to his practical side.] Hagrid, I understand how you feel, but keeping a dragon is illegal. You could get into serious trouble. Not to mention, your house is made of wood.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [This could be the perfect solution.] That's brilliant, Ron! (Turning to Hagrid) Hagrid, Charlie is an expert. He could make sure Norbert is well cared for and even released into the wild when he's ready.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [For once, I have no answer. I can't betray Hagrid, but I can't lie either.] (Stares at her slippers, trembling slightly)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I've never felt so ashamed in my life.] (Continues to stare at the floor, a tear rolling down her cheek)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [This sounds like a health issue.] Go to Madam Pomfrey.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I think I know what's causing Harry's anxiety.] That's just the exams. I woke up last night and was halfway through my Transfiguration notes before I remembered we'd done that one.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [We need to see Dumbledore, but how do we explain without revealing too much?] We want to see Professor Dumbledore.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [This is against every rule, but Harry seems determined.] You can't! After what McGonagall and Snape have said? You'll be expelled!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Harry's right. This is bigger than school rules.] You're right, Harry.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I'm sorry, Neville, but this is for the greater good.] Neville, I'm really, really sorry about this. Petrificus Totalus!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I recognize this plant from Herbology. We're in danger!] It's Devil's Snare! Don't move, it will only kill you faster!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Think, Hermione, think!] Devil's Snare, Devil's Snare... What did Professor Sprout say? It likes the dark and the damp —

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Of course! How could I forget?] Oh, right! (Casting a spell) Lumos Solem!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I hope Ron knows what he's doing.] How, exactly?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [We've faced challenges from different professors.] We've had Sprout's, that was the Devil's Snare; Flitwick must've put charms on the keys; McGonagall transfigured the chessmen to make them alive; that leaves Quirrell's spell, and Snape's...

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [This must be Snape's challenge.] (Reading a paper) It's a logic puzzle. Brilliant! This isn't magic — it's logic — a puzzle.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I can solve this. I need to focus.] Give me a minute.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [We've come so far, but Harry has to go alone now.] (Hugging Harry) Harry — you're a great wizard, you know.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Harry needs to understand his own worth.] Me! Books! And cleverness! There are more important things — friendship and bravery and — oh Harry — be careful!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I'm so glad he's okay, but I need to know what happened.] (looking concerned) Oh, Harry, we were so worried! What happened down there with Quirrell? Is it true about You-Know-Who?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [This is all so incredible. I have so many questions.] (looking thoughtful) Your mother's protection? That's fascinating magic. And what about the Stone? Is it safe?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I can't imagine making that choice, but I understand why they did it.] It's for the greater good, I suppose. But Harry, are you sure you're alright? You went through so much.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [We've been through so much already, but I know we can face whatever comes next.] (nodding firmly) Absolutely. We're in this together, Harry. Always.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [What could he mean by that?] (whispering excitedly) Oh! Do you think he means what happened with the Stone?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [This is overwhelming!] (burying her face in her arms, likely crying from emotion)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I need to prove myself. I've studied so hard for this moment.] (whispering rapidly) I've learned all our course books by heart, of course. I just hope it will be enough — I wonder which spell we'll need to perform.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I need to prove myself. I've studied so hard for this moment.] (whispering rapidly) I've learned all our course books by heart, of course. I just hope it will be enough — I wonder which spell we'll need to perform.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: (remains paralyzed against the wall, mouth open in terror)

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [They saved me. I can't believe it.] Is it — dead?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Snape's behavior is too suspicious to ignore.] But Snape's trying to steal it. I know a jinx when I see one, Hagrid. I've read all about them! You've got to keep eye contact, and Snape wasn't blinking at all, I saw him!

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Harry seems very anxious. This must be important.] (looking concerned) What's going on, Harry? Did something happen after the match?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [This confirms our suspicions about Snape, but why is Quirrell involved?] (gasping) So Snape is trying to steal the Stone! But why was he talking to Quirrell about it?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Oh no, this is terrible news.] (alarmed) But Quirrell's terrified of Snape! He won't be able to stand up to him for long.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [We need to be the voice of reason here.] But Hagrid, isn't dragon breeding illegal? This could get you into serious trouble.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [This is getting out of hand.] (concerned) Hagrid, how fast do Norwegian Ridgebacks grow, exactly?

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I can see how frightened Harry is, and I need to find a way to reassure him.] Harry, everyone says Dumbledore's the only one You-Know-Who was ever afraid of. With Dumbledore around, You-Know-Who won't touch you. Anyway, who says the centaurs are right? It sounds like fortune-telling to me, and Professor McGonagall says that's a very imprecise branch of magic.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [I'm worried about Harry's safety, but I also know we need to be cautious.] We should be careful, Harry. We don't want to get into any more trouble. But I agree, we need to stay alert.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [We're risking expulsion, but the Stone is more important.] Harry's right, it will be dangerous. But we're prepared, aren't we? We've learned so much this year.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [Oh, Ron.] (Rolls her eyes) Don't jinx it, Ron. We should be prepared for anything. I've been reviewing all our lessons, just in case.

utterances.book: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone (Harry Potter, #1)
utterances.message: [We need a plan.] Wait! (Pulls out her wand) We should have our wands ready. And Harry, you go first since you have the flute to put Fluffy to sleep.

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (Harry Potter, #2)
scenes.plot_summary: The day after Harry and Ron's dramatic arrival at Hogwarts in a flying car, they face the consequences of their actions. During breakfast in the Great Hall, Ron receives a Howler from his mother, delivered by the family's old owl Errol. The atmosphere is tense as they anticipate the contents of the red envelope.
scenes.scenario: The Great Hall buzzes with morning chatter as students gather for breakfast. Tensions linger from yesterday's dramatic events when Harry and Ron arrived at Hogwarts in a flying car, breaking school rules and risking exposure of the wizarding world. The mood is a mix of excitement and apprehension, with whispers about potential consequences circulating. Hermione, clearly disapproving, sits stiffly with an open book. As owls stream in with the daily mail, the air becomes charged with anticipation, especially around our trio of friends.
scenes.topic: Arrival of mail and Ron's Howler

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: Feeling a bit sheepish about yesterday's spectacle, Harry's grateful for the normalcy of breakfast but can't shake off worry about potential punishments. He's acutely aware of Hermione's disappointment and hopes to smooth things over with her. Despite everything, a part of him still feels a thrill from their adventure.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: Ron's stomach is in knots, dreading his parents' reaction to their flying car stunt. He's torn between pride in their daring feat and fear of the consequences, especially from his mother. As owls arrive, his anxiety peaks, hoping against hope that his family's owl isn't among them. He's not ready to face the music just yet.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: Hermione is deeply disappointed in Harry and Ron's reckless behavior. While worried about potential ramifications for her friends, she believes they need to understand the gravity of their actions. She's engrossed in her book partly to distract herself, partly to signal her disapproval. Despite her stern exterior, she's concerned for them.

dialogues.message: The Great Hall is filled with the usual breakfast chatter when suddenly, a rush of owls streams in, delivering letters and packages to the students.
[I hope Gran remembered to send the things I forgot.] Mail's due any minute—I think Gran's sending a few things I forgot.
[At least the food's good, even if the mood isn't.] (starts eating his porridge)
A big, lumpy package bounces off Neville's head, and something large and gray falls into Hermione's jug, spraying them all with milk and feathers.
[Oh no, it's Errol! And he's got a...] (pulling the bedraggled owl out by the feet) Errol!
[Is the owl okay?] (gently prodding Errol) It's all right, he's still alive.
[This is worse than I thought.] (gasping) Oh, no—
[What's wrong with Ron? The owl's alive, isn't it?] (looking concerned) What is it, Ron?
[Mum's sent a Howler. I'm done for.] (pointing at the red envelope) It's not that—it's that.
The red envelope lies ominously on the table, seeming to draw everyone's attention. The atmosphere becomes tense as the students nearby realize what it means.

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (Harry Potter, #2)
scenes.plot_summary: Harry attends his first Defense Against the Dark Arts class with the new professor, Gilderoy Lockhart. Lockhart proves to be incompetent, releasing Cornish pixies into the classroom and causing chaos. Harry and Ron are skeptical of Lockhart's abilities, while Hermione defends him.
scenes.scenario: It's the first Defense Against the Dark Arts class of the year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. The new professor, the charismatic celebrity author Gilderoy Lockhart, has just released a cage full of mischievous Cornish pixies into the classroom. The small, electric-blue creatures are causing havoc, destroying books, spraying ink, and lifting students into the air. The classroom is in utter chaos, with students ducking under desks and shielding themselves from the mayhem. Neville Longbottom hangs precariously from the chandelier, while other students frantically try to protect themselves and their belongings from the pixies' destruction.
scenes.topic: Dealing with the chaos caused by the pixies

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: Feeling frustrated and skeptical about Lockhart's teaching abilities. Wants to find a way to control the pixies and protect his classmates. Concerned about the chaos and Neville's safety. Annoyed by Lockhart's incompetence and theatrics. Ready to take action to resolve the situation.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: Angry and exasperated by Lockhart's incompetence. Skeptical of Lockhart's reputation and accomplishments. Wants to express his disbelief and criticism of the situation. Worried about the pixies' attacks and the destruction they're causing. Ready to confront Lockhart's inadequacy as a teacher.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: Conflicted between her admiration for Lockhart and the chaotic reality before her. Desperately wanting to believe in Lockhart's abilities and defend his actions. Determined to find a logical explanation for the situation. Prepared to take charge and solve the pixie problem herself if necessary.

key_characters.name: Gilderoy Lockhart
key_characters.thought: Panicking internally while trying to maintain his confident facade. Realizing he's out of his depth but unwilling to admit it. Searching for a way to save face and regain control of the situation. Hoping to delegate the problem to the students to avoid further embarrassment. Concerned about how this incident might affect his reputation.

dialogues.message: The classroom is in chaos. Pixies are flying everywhere, destroying books, spraying ink, and causing general mayhem. Neville Longbottom is dangling from the chandelier.
[I need to appear in control.] Come on now — round them up, round them up, they're only pixies! (He rolls up his sleeves and brandishes his wand)
[This spell should work... I think.] Peskipiksi Pesternomi! (He waves his wand dramatically)
The spell has no effect. One of the pixies seizes Lockhart's wand and throws it out of the window.

[This is embarrassing. I need to get out of here.] (He gulps and dives under his desk) Well, I'll ask you three to just nip the rest of them back into their cage. (He points at Harry, Ron, and Hermione before quickly leaving the room)
[I can't believe this!] Can you believe him? (A pixie bites his ear) Ouch!
[There must be a reasonable explanation for this.] He just wants to give us some hands-on experience. (She starts using a Freezing Charm on the pixies)
[Hermione can't be serious.] Hands on? Hermione, he didn't have a clue what he was doing— (He tries to grab a pixie)
[I need to defend Professor Lockhart.] Rubbish. You've read his books — look at all those amazing things he's done—
[This is ridiculous.] He says he's done. (He mutters under his breath)

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (Harry Potter, #2)
scenes.plot_summary: After discovering Mrs. Norris petrified and a mysterious message on the wall, Harry, Ron, and Hermione are questioned by Dumbledore and the teachers. In the following days, the school is abuzz with rumors about the Chamber of Secrets. During a History of Magic class, Professor Binns reluctantly explains the legend of the Chamber, revealing its connection to Salazar Slytherin and his desire to purge the school of Muggle-born students.
scenes.scenario: In the dimly lit History of Magic classroom at Hogwarts, students struggle to stay awake during Professor Binns' monotonous lecture. The ghost teacher drones on about goblin rebellions, his ethereal form barely visible in the flickering candlelight. The air is thick with boredom and the scratching of quills. Recent events have left the school on edge: a petrified cat, a chilling message on the wall, and whispers of the Chamber of Secrets. Tension and curiosity simmer beneath the surface as students yearn for answers about the mysterious happenings at their beloved school.
scenes.topic: The legend of the Chamber of Secrets

key_characters.name: Cuthbert Binns
key_characters.thought: Another day, another lecture. These students never change, always half-asleep. I must maintain the sanctity of historical facts. Why is that girl raising her hand? How unusual. I hope this interruption doesn't derail my carefully planned lesson on the goblin rebellion of 1612.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: I can't stand not knowing about the Chamber of Secrets anymore. The library had nothing concrete. Professor Binns must know something - he's been here for centuries! I have to ask, even if it means interrupting. This could be crucial to understanding what's happening at Hogwarts right now.

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I hope Hermione can get some information out of Binns. After what happened with Mrs. Norris and that writing on the wall, we need answers. Could this Chamber of Secrets have something to do with the strange voice I heard? I'm worried about what might happen next.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: Blimey, Hermione's actually going to interrupt Binns! This Chamber business must be serious. I hope we learn something useful - anything's better than another lecture on goblin wars. Maybe we'll finally find out what's going on around here.

dialogues.message: The classroom is filled with drowsy students, most of whom are barely paying attention to Professor Binns' droning lecture. Suddenly, Hermione's hand shoots up into the air, breaking the monotony.
[I need to phrase this carefully to get the information we need.] Professor, I was wondering if you could tell us anything about the Chamber of Secrets.
[This is most irregular. Why would a student be interested in such nonsense?] (looking amazed) Miss—er—?
Granger, Professor. I was wondering if you could tell us anything about the Chamber of Secrets.
The classroom suddenly comes to life. Students who were previously dozing off now sit up straight, their attention focused on Professor Binns and Hermione.
[I must maintain the academic integrity of my subject.] (blinking in surprise) My subject is History of Magic. I deal with facts, Miss Granger, not myths and legends.
[I won't give up that easily. There must be some factual basis to the legend.] (raising her hand again) Please, sir, don't legends always have a basis in fact?

[I've never encountered such persistence from a student before.] (looking at Hermione in amazement) Well, yes, one could argue that, I suppose. However, the legend of which you speak is such a very sensational, even ludicrous tale—
The entire class is now hanging on Professor Binns' every word, their faces turned towards him with rapt attention.
[I suppose I must satisfy their curiosity, if only to return to my lecture.] (sighing) Oh, very well. Let me see... the Chamber of Secrets...
[Finally, we might get some answers.] (leaning forward, listening intently)
[I can't believe we're actually getting Binns to talk about something interesting.] (exchanging excited glances with Harry)

[I shall present the facts as they are known.] You all know, of course, that Hogwarts was founded over a thousand years ago by the four greatest witches and wizards of the age: Godric Gryffindor, Helga Hufflepuff, Rowena Ravenclaw, and Salazar Slytherin...

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (Harry Potter, #2)
scenes.plot_summary: Harry and Ron discover a mysterious diary belonging to T.M. Riddle from 50 years ago, coinciding with the previous opening of the Chamber of Secrets. They investigate its significance and potential connection to the current attacks. Meanwhile, Lockhart organizes a Valentine's Day celebration at Hogwarts, much to the annoyance of other staff members.
scenes.scenario: It's a chilly evening in the Gryffindor common room. The fire crackles, casting warm light on the trio huddled in a corner. Recent attacks have left the school on edge, and the discovery of a mysterious diary has piqued their interest. The diary, found in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom, belonged to T.M. Riddle and is exactly 50 years old - coinciding with the last time the Chamber of Secrets was opened. Despite appearing blank, Harry feels an inexplicable connection to it. The friends have gathered to discuss its potential significance, each bringing their own perspective to the conversation.
scenes.topic: The significance of T.M. Riddle's diary and its potential connection to the Chamber of Secrets

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm convinced this diary is crucial to unraveling the Chamber of Secrets mystery. There's an odd familiarity about it that I can't explain. I need Ron and Hermione to understand its importance, even if it seems blank. Maybe together we can unlock its secrets.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: This whole diary business seems like a waste of time. We should be focusing on more tangible leads. I'm worried Harry's getting obsessed with this blank book, and I don't see how it could possibly help us. I want to protect my friends from potential dangers.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: The timing of this diary's discovery is too perfect to ignore. It could be our key to solving the Chamber of Secrets mystery. I'm eager to apply my knowledge and logical thinking to uncover any hidden information. We need to explore every possibility, no matter how unlikely it seems.

dialogues.message: [I need to convince them this is important.] Look, I know it seems useless, but I can't help feeling there's more to this diary.
[I don't see the point in all this.] (sighs) Harry, it's blank. What more could there be to it?
[This could be our breakthrough!] Actually, Ron, I think Harry might be onto something. The timing is too perfect to be a coincidence.
[I'm glad Hermione agrees.] Exactly! Riddle got an award 50 years ago, right when the Chamber was last opened.
[They're both going mad.] (looking skeptical) So what? Lots of students probably got awards that year.
[We need to consider all possibilities.] But what if Riddle got his award for catching the Heir of Slytherin? The diary could tell us everything!
[That makes sense!] (nodding enthusiastically) That would explain why someone tried to get rid of it.
[They're not listening to reason.] (exasperated) But there's nothing written in it! How can it tell us anything?
[There must be a way to reveal its secrets.] (pulls out her wand) It might be invisible ink. Aparecium!
Nothing happens to the diary pages after Hermione's spell.
[I'm not giving up yet.] (rummaging in her bag) I've got a Revealer, let me try that.
[This is pointless.] (rolling his eyes) I'm telling you, there's nothing to find in there. Riddle probably just got a diary for Christmas and couldn't be bothered filling it in.
[I can't explain it, but I feel connected to this diary somehow.] (looking thoughtful) Maybe, but I still think it's worth looking into. I can't explain why, but this diary means something.

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (Harry Potter, #7)
scenes.plot_summary: Harry prepares to leave Privet Drive for the last time. Members of the Order arrive to escort him safely. They use Polyjuice Potion to create seven Harry decoys. During their flight, they are ambushed by Death Eaters. In the ensuing battle, Harry's owl Hedwig is killed, and he loses his wand. Voldemort personally pursues Harry, but Harry's wand acts of its own accord, driving Voldemort away. The chase ends with Harry and Hagrid crash-landing.
scenes.scenario: A group of wizards has gathered to enact a risky plan to protect Harry Potter. They are in a tense kitchen meeting, discussing using a magical potion to create decoys. The atmosphere is serious but some try to lighten the mood with jokes. Harry is reluctant about others risking themselves, while the adults insist it's necessary. They need Harry's cooperation to proceed with the plan.
scenes.topic: The plan to use Polyjuice Potion and create Harry decoys

key_characters.name: Alastor Moody
key_characters.thought: I must take charge and ensure this critical plan is executed properly, despite any objections. Time is of the essence and we cannot afford mistakes or hesitation.

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm deeply uncomfortable with others putting themselves in danger for me. I want to refuse but feel conflicted, knowing the stakes are high. I need to voice my concerns while grappling with the reality of the situation.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: This plan is our best option logically, even if it's dangerous. I'm worried about Harry's reaction and hope he'll understand the necessity. We need to support him through this difficult decision.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: This whole situation is mental, but I trust the Order knows what they're doing. I want to support Harry and keep things from getting too heavy, even if I'm nervous myself about what's to come.

dialogues.message: [I need to present this plan firmly and decisively to prevent any arguments.] We're using Polyjuice Potion. (He pulls out a flask of muddy liquid) There will be seven Harry Potters moving through the skies tonight, each with a companion.
[I can't believe what I'm hearing. This is too dangerous for them.] No! (He says loudly) I won't let six people risk their lives --
[I need to lighten the mood a bit.] (Smirking) Because it's the first time for all of us, mate.
[They don't understand how serious this is.] This is different, pretending to be me --
[A joke might help ease the tension.] Well, none of us really fancy it, Harry. (He says earnestly) Imagine if something went wrong and we were stuck as specky, scrawny gits forever.
[I appreciate the attempt at humor, but this is too serious.] (He doesn't smile) You can't do it if I don't cooperate. You need me to give you some hair.
[Harry's being stubborn. Time for more sarcasm.] Well, that's the plan scuppered. Obviously there's no chance at all of us getting a bit of your hair unless you cooperate.
[Joining in with George's sarcasm.] Yeah, thirteen of us against one bloke who's not allowed to use magic; we've got no chance.
[Their jokes aren't helping. I need to make them understand how dangerous this is.] Funny. (He says flatly) Really amusing.

[Enough of this banter. We need to move forward with the plan.] (His voice becomes a growl) If it has to come to force, then it will. Everyone here's overage, Potter, and they're all prepared to take the risk.
The kitchen falls silent as the gravity of Moody's words sinks in. The tension in the air is palpable as everyone waits for Harry's response.
[I hate this, but I know they won't back down. I have to agree for their sake.] (He glances at Ron, who grimaces encouragingly) Fine. But I still think it's mad.
[Finally, we can proceed.] Good. (He limps forward, uncorking the flask) Now, some of your hair, please, Potter.
[This feels wrong, but I have no choice.] (Reluctantly, he reaches up and pulls out a hank of hair)

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (Harry Potter, #7)
scenes.plot_summary: Harry, Ron, and Hermione escape from Bill and Fleur's wedding after Death Eaters attack. They flee to Tottenham Court Road, change clothes, and are attacked by Death Eaters in a café. After defeating them and wiping their memories, the trio decides to hide at Grimmauld Place. There, they encounter magical traps left for Snape and experience a vision of Voldemort torturing Rowle.
scenes.scenario: The trio has just apparated into the gloomy hallway of 12 Grimmauld Place, former headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix. They're on edge after narrowly escaping a Death Eater attack at Bill and Fleur's wedding and another ambush at a café. The house is dark and foreboding, with flickering gas lamps casting eerie shadows. They're unsure if it's truly safe, worried about potential traps left for Snape, and anxious about the fate of their friends and family. The weight of their sudden isolation and the dangerous mission ahead hangs heavily in the air.
scenes.topic: Safety concerns and next steps at Grimmauld Place

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm torn between relief at finding shelter and guilt for endangering Ron and Hermione. We need a plan, but first, we must ensure this place is secure. I'm worried about everyone at the wedding and frustrated by our limited options. The responsibility of leading this mission weighs on me, and I'm determined to find a way forward.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: My mind is racing, analyzing potential threats and protective measures. I'm anxious about our safety and the well-being of those we left behind. We need to thoroughly check the house for dangers and establish our next steps. I'm scared but trying to stay focused and logical for the group's sake.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: I'm overwhelmed with fear for my family's safety and guilt for leaving them behind. Part of me wonders if coming here was the right choice, but I trust Harry and Hermione. I'm trying to stay alert and be useful, despite feeling out of my depth. I want to comfort Hermione but I'm barely holding it together myself.

dialogues.message: The trio enters the dark and eerie hallway of Grimmauld Place. Old-fashioned gas lamps flicker to life, casting shadows along the walls.
[I need to stay alert and look for any signs of danger.] (whispering and pointing) I think somebody's been in here.
[Could it be the Order? Or someone worse?] (murmuring) That could've happened as the Order left.
[We need to be cautious, but we can't just stand here forever.] So where are these jinxes they put up against Snape?
[That's a good point. Maybe we're safe after all?] Maybe they're only activated if he shows up?
[We need to move forward, despite the risks.] Well, we can't stay here forever. (takes a step forward)
Suddenly, Mad-Eye Moody's voice whispers out of the darkness, startling the trio.
[Panic rises in me, but I need to stay calm.] (croaking) We're not Snape!
[That must be one of the protective spells. I hope there aren't more dangerous ones.] (stammering) That m-must have b-been the T-Tongue-Tying Curse Mad-Eye set up for Snape!
A terrifying dust figure rises from the carpet, resembling Dumbledore, and glides towards them.
[Terror grips me, but I know we're innocent.] (shouting) No! It wasn't us! We didn't kill you –
The figure explodes into a cloud of dust as Harry says the word 'kill'.
[That was horrifying, but I need to comfort Hermione.] (shakily) It's all r-right... It's g-gone...
[We need to make sure we're truly alone and safe.] (whispering) Before we go any farther, I think we'd better check. (raises her wand) Homenum revelio.

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows (Harry Potter, #7)
scenes.plot_summary: Harry, Ron, and Hermione are waiting for Kreacher to return with Mundungus Fletcher. Meanwhile, they learn from Lupin about the dire situation in the wizarding world under Voldemort's control. Kreacher finally returns with Mundungus, who reveals he gave away the locket to a Ministry woman who looked like a toad, likely Dolores Umbridge.
scenes.scenario: In the kitchen of Grimmauld Place, tension fills the air as Harry, Ron, and Hermione prepare to interrogate Mundungus Fletcher about Slytherin's locket. The trio has been hiding out in this gloomy, once-abandoned house while pursuing their secret mission from Dumbledore. Kreacher, the house-elf now loyal to Harry, has just brought in a disheveled and nervous Mundungus. The kitchen is dimly lit, with ancient cooking implements hanging from the walls. The weight of their quest and the dangers of the outside world under Voldemort's growing power press heavily on their minds as they face this crucial moment in their search for Horcruxes.
scenes.topic: The whereabouts of Slytherin's locket

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I must control my anger and focus on getting the truth about the locket. This could be our only lead to finding a Horcrux. I'm worried about what Mundungus might have done with it, but I need to stay calm and assertive. The fate of the wizarding world might depend on this information.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: I'm ready to support Harry however I can. Mundungus is a slippery character, but we need to get this information out of him. I'll keep an eye on Harry's temper and be prepared to step in if needed. We can't let this opportunity slip away.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: We need to approach this interrogation carefully. Mundungus is untrustworthy, but intimidation might not be the best strategy. I'll observe closely and intervene if things get out of hand. We must get the information about the locket without alienating a potential ally against Voldemort.

key_characters.name: Mundungus Fletcher
key_characters.thought: I'm in deep trouble here. These kids look dead serious, and that house-elf seems ready to bash my head in. I need to find a way out of this mess without revealing too much. Maybe I can talk my way out or pretend I don't know anything important.

dialogues.message: [I need to establish control immediately.] (points his wand at Mundungus) You're not in much of a position to make threats. When you cleaned out this house of anything valuable -
[Maybe I can deflect this somehow.] (interrupts hastily) Sirius never cared about any of the junk -
There's a sudden commotion as Kreacher takes a run at Mundungus, hitting him over the head with a saucepan.
[Bloody hell, that hurt!] (screams in pain) Call 'im off, call 'im off, 'e should be locked up!
[I need Mundungus conscious, but Kreacher's loyalty is touching.] Kreacher, no! (turns to the house-elf) We need him conscious, Kreacher, but if he needs persuading, you can do the honors.
[I'm pleased to be of service to Master Harry.] (bows low) Thank you very much, Master. (retreats but keeps glaring at Mundungus)

[Let's try this again.] When you stripped this house of all the valuables you could find, you took a bunch of stuff from the kitchen cupboard. There was a locket there. (swallows nervously) What did you do with it?
[They're after that locket? Must be valuable.] (looks curious) Why? Is it valuable?
[He still has it!] (exclaims excitedly) You've still got it!
[Mundungus is too greedy to have kept it.] (says shrewdly) No, he hasn't. He's wondering whether he should have asked more money for it.
[Might as well tell them the truth now.] (looks defeated) More? That wouldn't have been effing difficult... bleedin' gave it away, din' I? No choice.
