scenes.scenario: In a dimly lit room at 12 Grimmauld Place, the secret headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix, tensions are high. Harry Potter has just arrived after being kept in the dark all summer about Voldemort's return. The musty air is thick with unspoken words and suppressed emotions. Ron and Hermione, looking guilty and anxious, face a visibly upset Harry. The creaky floorboards and peeling wallpaper of the old house seem to reflect the strained atmosphere. Outside, the muffled sounds of London traffic serve as a stark contrast to the magical world's troubles discussed within these walls.
scenes.topic: The Order of the Phoenix and recent events

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: Conflicted between anger at being left out and relief at finally being with his friends. Desperate for information about Voldemort and the Order. Feeling betrayed but also curious. Wants to understand why he was kept isolated all summer.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: Guilty about keeping Harry in the dark. Anxious to explain without revealing too much. Worried about Harry's reaction and their friendship. Wants to share information about his family, especially Percy's situation. Hoping Harry will understand their position.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: Torn between loyalty to Dumbledore and empathy for Harry. Eager to provide logical explanations. Concerned about the bigger picture of Voldemort's return and the Ministry's stance. Wants to reassure Harry while adhering to the promise of secrecy.

key_characters.name: Fred Weasley
key_characters.thought: Amused by the tense situation but also sympathetic to Harry. Eager to lighten the mood with humor. Curious about Harry's reaction to recent events. Ready to share some information about the Order's activities within limits.

key_characters.name: George Weasley
key_characters.thought: Aligned with Fred in wanting to ease the tension. Prepared to offer insights about the Order and family matters. Slightly concerned about the seriousness of the situation but maintaining a jovial exterior. Interested in Harry's perspective on recent events.

dialogues.message: [I need to calm down and get some answers.] (Takes a deep breath) What is this place anyway?
[Finally, something I can answer without breaking any promises.] Headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix.
[The Order of the what?] Is anyone going to bother telling me what the Order of the Phoenix — ?
[I should explain this quickly before Harry gets upset again.] It's a secret society. Dumbledore's in charge, he founded it. It's the people who fought against You-Know-Who last time.
[A secret society? Why wasn't I told about this before?] Who's in it?
[We can't give too many details, but...] Quite a few people —
[We should give him some idea of the scale.] — we've met about twenty of them, but we think there are more...
[They're still being vague.] (Glares at them) Well? (Looks from one to the other)
[What does he mean?] Er... Well what?
[Why do I have to spell everything out?] Voldemort! (Ron and Hermione wince) What's happening? What's he up to? Where is he? What are we doing to stop him?
[I wish we could tell him more.] We've told you, the Order don't let us in on their meetings. So we don't know the details — but we've got a general idea —
With two loud cracks, Fred and George materialize out of thin air in the middle of the room, startling everyone.
[Harry's voice could wake the dead.] (Beaming) Hello, Harry. We thought we heard your dulcet tones.
[Better lighten the mood a bit.] You don't want to bottle up your anger like that, Harry, let it all out. There might be a couple of people fifty miles away who didn't hear you.
[Great, more people who know more than me.] (Grumpily) You two passed your Apparation tests, then?

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.chapter: The Noble and Most Ancient House of Black
scenes.plot_summary: The next morning, Harry and the others are tasked with cleaning the drawing room of Grimmauld Place, which is infested with doxies. They encounter various magical pests and objects, highlighting the state of neglect in the Black family home. Sirius mentions caring for Buckbeak upstairs and identifies a potential boggart in a cabinet.
scenes.scenario: In the dilapidated drawing room of 12 Grimmauld Place, the hidden headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix, a group of wizards prepares to tackle a severe magical pest infestation. The once-grand Black family home is now a neglected, gloomy space filled with dark artifacts and magical creatures. Tensions linger from recent arguments about Harry's involvement in Order affairs. The room is cluttered with dusty furniture, and the walls are adorned with faded tapestries. A locked cabinet shakes ominously, hinting at dangerous contents. The atmosphere is thick with anticipation and a touch of apprehension as they face the unknown perils of cleaning this magically contaminated space.
scenes.topic: Cleaning the drawing room and dealing with magical pests

key_characters.name: Molly Weasley
key_characters.thought: I'm determined to make this house safe and habitable, but I'm worried about the children's safety. The tension with Sirius over Harry's involvement in Order matters is still fresh in my mind. I need to stay focused and keep everyone on task, despite the potential dangers lurking in this old house. It's crucial to maintain a calm demeanor to not alarm the children further.

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm fascinated by Sirius's family home and eager to learn more about my godfather's past. However, I'm also frustrated by being kept in the dark about Order business and worried about my upcoming disciplinary hearing. The cleaning task seems tedious, but it might provide an opportunity to overhear something important. I'm torn between curiosity about the house and anxiety about recent events.

key_characters.name: Sirius Black
key_characters.thought: Being back in my childhood home brings up painful memories and a sense of confinement. I'm eager to be useful to the Order but feel trapped and restless. I want to connect with Harry and provide guidance, but I'm conflicted about how much to reveal. The state of the house reflects my own inner turmoil, and I'm both resentful of and responsible for its condition. I'm trying to balance being helpful with my deep-seated desire to rebel against my family's legacy.

dialogues.message: [I need to make sure everyone is prepared for this task.] Cover your faces and take a spray. (points to bottles of black liquid) It's Doxycide. I've never seen an infestation this bad — what that house-elf's been doing for the last ten years —

[I feel the need to defend Kreacher, even if others don't understand.] (face half-concealed by a tea towel, throws a reproachful look at Mrs. Weasley) Kreacher's really old, he probably couldn't manage —

[I need to correct Hermione's misconception about Kreacher.] (enters the room carrying a bloodstained bag) You'd be surprised what Kreacher can manage when he wants to, Hermione. I've just been feeding Buckbeak. (notices Harry's inquiring look) I keep him upstairs in my mother's bedroom. Anyway... this writing desk...
Sirius drops the bag of rats onto an armchair and bends over to examine a locked cabinet that is shaking slightly.

[I should warn them about potential dangers in the house.] Well, Molly, I'm pretty sure this is a boggart, but perhaps we ought to let Mad-Eye have a shifty at it before we let it out — knowing my mother it could be something much worse.
[I agree with Sirius, but I'm still feeling tense from our argument last night.] Right you are, Sirius.
A loud, clanging bell sounds from downstairs, followed by screams and wails.
[I'm exasperated by the constant disruptions in this house.] I keep telling them not to ring the doorbell! (hurries out of the room)
[I need to keep the children focused on the task at hand.] Close the door, please, Harry.
[I'm curious about what's happening downstairs, but I don't want to upset Mrs. Weasley.] (takes his time closing the door, trying to listen to the conversation downstairs)

[I need to prepare everyone for dealing with the doxies.] (bends over to check a book) Right, you lot, you need to be careful, because doxies bite and their teeth are poisonous. I've got a bottle of antidote here, but I'd rather nobody needed it.

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: Harry notices Sirius's mood worsening after learning Harry will return to Hogwarts. The Hogwarts letters arrive, revealing that Ron and Hermione have been made prefects, not Harry. This surprises everyone, especially Fred and George. Mrs. Weasley is overjoyed and promises Ron a reward. Harry struggles with feelings of jealousy and disappointment but ultimately congratulates Ron.
scenes.scenario: In the dimly lit bedroom of 12 Grimmauld Place, the headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix, tension and excitement fill the air as Harry, Ron, Hermione, Fred, and George gather around their newly arrived Hogwarts letters. The room is cluttered with magical objects and old furniture, creating a somewhat claustrophobic atmosphere. The group has been spending their summer cleaning the ancient Black family home, and this moment of normalcy - receiving their school letters - brings a mix of anticipation and apprehension. Unbeknownst to them, these letters contain surprising news that will shift the dynamic of their friend group and challenge their expectations for the upcoming school year.
scenes.topic: Reaction to Ron being made prefect

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm anxious about returning to Hogwarts after the events of last year. Being made prefect would be a nice validation, but I'm also worried about Sirius being left alone. I hope there's good news in these letters to lift everyone's spirits.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: I'm nervous about what's in these letters. Being overshadowed by my brothers and Harry is frustrating, but I don't expect anything special for myself. I'm curious to see who made prefect, probably Harry and Hermione.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: I'm excited but nervous about the contents of our letters. Being made prefect would be a dream come true, but I'm also concerned about how it might affect our friendship dynamics, especially if Harry or Ron don't get the position.

key_characters.name: Fred Weasley
key_characters.thought: Another year, another chance for mischief. These letters are always good for a laugh, especially seeing who they've made prefect this time. I bet it's Harry - that'll be interesting to see how it changes things around here.

key_characters.name: George Weasley
key_characters.thought: I'm looking forward to seeing everyone's reactions to the letters. It's always amusing to see who gets stuck with prefect duties. I'm hoping for some surprising news to liven up the mood in this gloomy place.

dialogues.message: The bedroom at Grimmauld Place is filled with a mix of excitement and tension as the Hogwarts letters are opened and the prefect badges are revealed.
[I can't believe this is happening. Is this real?] (Staring at his letter in disbelief) I'm... I'm a prefect?
[This has to be a joke.] No way. (Snatching the letter) There's been a mistake. No one in their right mind would make Ron a prefect.
[This is too good to be true.] (Grinning mischievously) We thought you were a cert, Harry! What with winning the Triwizard and everything.
[I feel a mix of shock and disappointment, but I need to hide it.] (Forcing a smile) Well done, Ron. That's really great.
[I'm excited but also concerned about Harry's reaction.] (Entering the room breathlessly) Did you get - Oh! Ron, you're prefect too? That's wonderful!
[I'm still in disbelief, but starting to feel proud.] Yeah, it's my name on the letter. Can't quite believe it myself.
Mrs. Weasley enters the room, unaware of the news, carrying freshly laundered robes.
[I wonder what all the commotion is about.] What's going on here? (Noticing the badges) Ron, you're not...?
[Here goes nothing.] (Holding up his badge) Yeah, Mum. I'm a prefect.
[I'm overwhelmed with pride and joy!] (Shrieking with delight) I don't believe it! Oh, Ron, how wonderful! A prefect! That's everyone in the family!
[Feeling a bit left out.] (Sarcastically) What are Fred and I, next-door neighbors?
[I'm trying to be happy for Ron, but I can't help feeling left out.] (Quietly) Congratulations again, Ron. You deserve it.

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: Harry and his friends receive their Hogwarts letters, with Ron and Hermione being made prefects. This leads to a celebratory dinner, where Harry sees an old photo of the original Order of the Phoenix. Later, he encounters Mrs. Weasley struggling with a boggart that takes the form of her dead family members, revealing her deep fears about the ongoing conflict.
scenes.scenario: It's late summer at 12 Grimmauld Place, headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix. Harry, Ron and Hermione are in a bedroom when their Hogwarts letters arrive, bringing unexpected news. The mood is a mix of excitement and tension, as the friends process the surprise of Ron being named prefect instead of Harry. The worn, creaky house creates an atmosphere of secrecy and anticipation as they prepare to return to school amid growing dangers in the wizarding world.
scenes.topic: Ron being chosen as prefect

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: Feeling conflicted - happy for Ron but disappointed and confused about not being chosen himself. Wondering about Dumbledore's decision and trying to mask his hurt. Wants to be supportive of his friends despite his inner turmoil.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: Shocked and elated at being named prefect, something he never expected. Excited but also nervous about living up to the responsibility. Concerned about Harry's reaction and hoping this won't affect their friendship.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: Proud of her own prefect status but surprised by Ron's appointment. Trying to balance her excitement with sensitivity to Harry's feelings. Eager to discuss prefect duties but unsure how to navigate the unexpected situation.

dialogues.message: [I can't believe it's me. I'm sure Harry expected to get it.] (stares at his prefect badge in disbelief) I never thought it would be me! I thought it would be you!
[I need to be supportive, even if I'm feeling disappointed.] Nah, I've caused too much trouble. (forces a smile) Well done, mate.
[I'm excited but also concerned about Harry's reaction.] (enters the room excitedly) Did you — did you get — ? (spots the badge in Harry's hand) I knew it! Me too, Harry, me too!
[I need to correct her assumption quickly.] No, it's Ron, not me. (pushes the badge back into Ron's hand)
[I'm surprised, but I need to be supportive of Ron.] (looks bewildered) Ron? But... are you sure? I mean —
[I feel a bit defensive about her reaction.] (looks at Hermione with a defiant expression) It's my name on the letter.
[I need to recover from my surprise and show support.] (blushes) I... well... wow! Well done, Ron! That's really —
[I can't resist teasing Ron about this.] (enters the room with Fred) Unexpected.
[I need to defend Ron from his brothers' teasing.] (blushes harder) No, no, it's not... Ron's done loads of... he's really...
The door opens wider and Mrs. Weasley enters, carrying freshly laundered robes.

[I'm so proud of Ron, but I need to tend to everyone's needs.] Ginny said the booklists had come at last. (glances around at the envelopes) If you give them to me I'll take them over to Diagon Alley this afternoon and get your books while you're packing.

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: Harry, Ginny, and Neville are joined by Ron and Hermione, who share news about prefects. Luna Lovegood makes an odd impression. Harry reads The Quibbler, finding strange articles including one about Sirius Black. Malfoy taunts Harry about being a prefect. As they arrive at Hogwarts, Harry notices strange horse-like creatures pulling the carriages, which Ron can't see.
scenes.scenario: It's the start of a new term at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. The Hogwarts Express is speeding through the countryside, carrying students back to school. In a compartment, Harry Potter, Ginny Weasley, and Neville Longbottom are joined by Luna Lovegood, a Ravenclaw student known for her eccentric behavior. The atmosphere is filled with a mix of excitement and tension as they await the return of Ron and Hermione from the prefects' meeting. The compartment is cramped, filled with trunks, owl cages, and the scent of chocolate frogs. Outside, the landscape rushes by, a blur of green fields and occasional villages.
scenes.topic: New prefects and Luna's odd behavior

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: I'm exhausted from the prefects' meeting and starving. Can't wait to tell Harry about being made prefect, though I'm a bit nervous about the responsibilities. Hope I can handle it all. Maybe I can use this position to get back at Malfoy and his cronies.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: I'm proud to be a prefect but disappointed in some of the choices, especially Malfoy and Pansy. I hope Ron takes this seriously and doesn't abuse his position. I'm worried about how Harry might feel about not being chosen. We need to be sensitive about it.

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm curious about the prefect news, but I can't help feeling a bit left out and jealous. Why wasn't I chosen? I try to be happy for Ron and Hermione, but it's hard. I'm also dreading the potential confrontation with Malfoy, especially after the events of last year.

key_characters.name: Luna Lovegood
key_characters.thought: This is an interesting group. I feel a bit out of place, but I'm glad to be included. I wonder if they know about the latest discoveries in The Quibbler. Maybe I can share some insights if the conversation allows. I hope they don't think I'm too strange.

dialogues.message: [I'm exhausted and famished. I need to eat something before I share the news.] (stows Pigwidgeon next to Hedwig, grabs a Chocolate Frog from Harry and throws himself into the seat) I'm starving. (bites off the Frog's head and leans back with his eyes closed)
[I should give them an overview of the prefect situation.] Well, there are two fifth-year prefects from each House. Boy and girl from each. (looks thoroughly disgruntled as she takes her seat)
[I bet Harry can guess who the Slytherin prefect is.] And guess who's a Slytherin prefect? (still with his eyes closed)
[It's obvious, isn't it?] (with a sinking feeling) Malfoy.
[Of course it's Malfoy. Typical.] 'Course. (bitterly, stuffing the rest of the Frog into his mouth and taking another)
[I can't believe Pansy got chosen. She's completely unqualified.] And that complete cow Pansy Parkinson. How she got to be a prefect when she's thicker than a concussed troll... (says viciously)
[I wonder about the other houses.] Who's Hufflepuff?
[At least the Hufflepuff choices are decent.] (thickly) Ernie Macmillan and Hannah Abbott.
[I should mention the Ravenclaw prefects too.] And Anthony Goldstein and Padma Patil for Ravenclaw.
[Oh, I remember something about Ron and Padma.] (in a vague voice) You went to the Yule Ball with Padma Patil.
[Why is she bringing that up?] (swallows his mouthful of Frog, looking mildly surprised) Yeah, I know I did.

[I should share what I know about that night.] She didn't enjoy it very much. She doesn't think you treated her very well, because you wouldn't dance with her. I don't think I'd have minded. (adds thoughtfully) I don't like dancing very much.

An awkward silence falls over the compartment. Ron stares at Luna with his mouth hanging open, then looks around at Ginny for some kind of explanation. Ginny has stuffed her knuckles in her mouth to stop herself from giggling.

[That was... unexpected. I should change the subject.] (shakes his head, bemused, then checks his watch) We're supposed to patrol the corridors every so often, and we can give out punishments if people are misbehaving. I can't wait to get Crabbe and Goyle for something...

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: Harry notices strange horse-like creatures pulling the carriages to Hogwarts, which only he and Luna can see. At the Great Hall, they discuss Hagrid's absence and notice a new staff member, Dolores Umbridge. The Sorting Hat sings an unusual song warning of danger and urging unity among the houses.
scenes.scenario: It's the start of a new year at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. The students have just arrived at Hogsmeade station and are boarding carriages to take them to the castle. The night air is cool and crisp, filled with excitement and anticipation. Harry Potter, still reeling from the events of the previous year and his encounter with Voldemort, notices something strange about the carriages. Invisible to most, skeletal horse-like creatures are pulling them. This unsettling sight, combined with the conspicuous absence of their friend and teacher Hagrid, creates an atmosphere of unease and mystery as the friends settle into their carriage for the short journey to the castle.
scenes.topic: The mysterious horse-like creatures and Hagrid's absence

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm feeling anxious and confused. These horse-like creatures weren't here before - why can I see them now? And where's Hagrid? Everything feels off, and I can't shake this sense of unease. I need to find out what's going on, but I don't want to worry Ron and Hermione more than necessary.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: Harry's acting strange, and I'm getting worried. First these invisible horses he's talking about, and now Hagrid's missing. Something doesn't feel right. I want to lighten the mood, but I'm not sure how. Maybe changing the subject will help?

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: I'm concerned about Harry and Hagrid. Harry seems genuinely distressed about these creatures he's seeing, and Hagrid's absence is troubling. There must be a logical explanation for all of this. I need to gather more information and perhaps do some research when we get to the castle.

key_characters.name: Luna Lovegood
key_characters.thought: It's nice to see the thestrals again. I wonder why Harry can suddenly see them now? He seems upset, but it's actually quite special to be able to see them. I hope I can help him understand and feel better about it. Maybe we can become friends?

dialogues.message: [I need to make sure I'm not imagining things.] (looking anxiously at Ron) Can't you see what's pulling the carriages?
[Harry's really worrying me now.] (looks bemused) What are you talking about? There's nothing pulling the carriages, Harry. They're moving by themselves like always.
[This is frustrating. I know I'm seeing something!] (insistently) But there are creatures there! They look like horses, but... skeletal. Can't you see them?
[This is concerning. Harry's never mentioned seeing these creatures before.] (frowning) Harry, are you feeling alright? Maybe you should see Madam Pomfrey when we get to the castle.
[I should reassure Harry. He looks quite distressed.] (in a dreamy voice) Don't worry, you're not going mad or anything. I can see them too.
[Finally, someone else sees them!] (turning to Luna with relief) You can? What are they?
[It's nice to share this with someone else.] They're called Thestrals. They've always been pulling the carriages, but they can only be seen by people who've seen death.
[This is getting weird. I need to change the subject.] (uncomfortably) Er, right. Did anyone see that Grubbly-Plank woman? What's she doing back here? Hagrid can't have left, can he?
[I'm worried about Hagrid too, but I don't want to jump to conclusions.] (biting her lip) I hope he's alright. Maybe he's just... delayed for some reason?
[I hope Hagrid's okay. Maybe it's related to his mission for Dumbledore?] (quietly) Maybe he's not back yet from his mission - you know, the thing he was doing over the summer for Dumbledore.
[I should share my opinion, even if they might not agree.] I'll be quite glad if he has left. He isn't a very good teacher, is he?
An awkward silence falls over the carriage. Harry, Ron, and Hermione exchange uncomfortable glances, clearly disagreeing with Luna's assessment but unsure how to respond politely.

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: Harry faces continued skepticism about Voldemort's return, particularly from Seamus. He, Ron, and Hermione discuss the challenges of their fifth year, including O.W.L. exams and new teachers. They attend their first History of Magic class and discuss future career aspirations.
scenes.scenario: It's breakfast time in the Great Hall at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. The air is filled with excitement and anxiety as students begin their fifth year, facing the daunting O.W.L. exams. Harry, Ron, and Hermione sit at the Gryffindor table, examining their new schedules. The weight of recent events, including skepticism about Voldemort's return, hangs over them. The hall buzzes with chatter about the challenges ahead and the mysterious new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher, Professor Umbridge. Amidst this atmosphere, Fred and George Weasley spot an opportunity to promote their latest mischievous inventions.
scenes.topic: The difficulties of fifth year and Fred and George's joke shop plans

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: Feeling frustrated by the skepticism he's facing, Harry tries to focus on the upcoming year. He's worried about the increased workload and new challenges, especially with the tension from classmates like Seamus. He wants to discuss these concerns with his friends and seek their support.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: Overwhelmed by the difficult schedule ahead, Ron feels a mix of dread and curiosity about Fred and George's products. He's torn between his prefect duties and the temptation to find an easy way out. He wants to share his concerns about the year ahead with Harry and Hermione.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: Determined to face the challenges of fifth year head-on, Hermione is irritated by Fred and George's disruptive plans. She's worried about Harry and wants to keep both him and Ron focused on their studies. She's ready to assert her authority as a prefect to maintain order.

key_characters.name: Fred Weasley
key_characters.thought: Excited about the potential market for their products, Fred sees the stressed fifth-years as perfect customers. He's eager to promote the Skiving Snackboxes and test the limits of what they can get away with. He wants to convince the trio of the benefits of their inventions.

key_characters.name: George Weasley
key_characters.thought: Sharing Fred's enthusiasm for their products, George is also cautious about revealing too much about their business, especially their funding source. He's ready to use the stress of O.W.L. year as a selling point and wants to challenge Hermione's authority while avoiding outright confrontation.

dialogues.message: [This schedule looks awful. Maybe Fred and George have a point.] (groaning) Look at today! History of Magic, double Potions, Divination, and double Defense Against the Dark Arts... Binns, Snape, Trelawney, and that Umbridge woman all in one day! I wish Fred and George'd hurry up and get those Skiving Snackboxes sorted...
[Perfect timing!] (arriving with George) Do mine ears deceive me? Hogwarts prefects surely don't wish to skive off lessons?
[Maybe they can help after all.] (shoving his schedule under Fred's nose) Look what we've got today. That's the worst Monday I've ever seen.
[This is our chance to make a sale.] Fair point, little bro. (scanning the column) You can have a bit of Nosebleed Nougat cheap if you like.
[That sounds too good to be true.] (suspiciously) Why's it cheap?
[Honesty is the best policy... sort of.] (helping himself to a kipper) Because you'll keep bleeding till you shrivel up, we haven't got an antidote yet.
[Maybe not such a good idea after all.] (moodily) Cheers, but I think I'll take the lessons.
[I need to put a stop to this.] (eyeing Fred and George beadily) And speaking of your Skiving Snackboxes, you can't advertise for testers on the Gryffindor notice board.
[Challenge accepted.] (looking astonished) Says who?
[I need to assert my authority.] Says me. And Ron.
[I don't want to be involved in this.] (hastily) Leave me out of it.

[She'll come around eventually.] (thickly buttering a crumpet) You'll be singing a different tune soon enough, Hermione. You're starting your fifth year, you'll be begging us for a Snackbox before long.
[They can't be serious.] And why would starting fifth year mean I want a Skiving Snackbox?
[Time to scare them a bit.] Fifth year's O.W.L. year. Half our year had minor breakdowns coming up to O.W.L.s. Tears and tantrums... Patricia Stimpson kept coming over faint...
[This conversation is getting out of hand. I need to change the subject.] (deciding to steer the conversation away) D'you reckon it's true this year's going to be really tough? Because of the exams?

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: This plot covers several key events at Hogwarts as the new school year begins. It includes discussions about Quidditch team changes, the arrival of owls with mail, and the start of classes. The students face challenging courses, especially Potions with Snape and Defense Against the Dark Arts with the new professor, Umbridge. There are tensions between Harry, Ron, and Hermione, as well as concerns about the upcoming O.W.L. exams.
scenes.scenario: It's the start of a new school year at Hogwarts, and tensions are high among the fifth-year students. The Great Hall buzzes with activity as students discuss their challenging class schedules and the arrival of a new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher, Professor Umbridge. The pressure of the upcoming O.W.L. exams looms over everyone, particularly affecting Harry, Ron, and Hermione. Recent events, including Harry's claims about Voldemort's return, have created a tense atmosphere throughout the wizarding world, which is palpable even within the school's walls.
scenes.topic: Concerns about O.W.L. year and Professor Umbridge

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: Feeling overwhelmed by the upcoming year and frustrated with his friends' constant bickering. Anxious about facing Snape in Potions and curious about the new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher. Struggling with the weight of recent events and the skepticism he faces about Voldemort's return.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: Worried about the difficulty of their classes and the impending O.W.L. exams. Feeling the pressure of his new prefect responsibilities while also desiring to find ways to avoid the workload. Concerned about the Quidditch team changes and how they might affect his chances of playing.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: Determined to excel in her studies and take the O.W.L. year seriously. Frustrated by Ron's apparent lack of dedication to his prefect duties and academic responsibilities. Curious but apprehensive about Professor Umbridge's teaching methods and the implications for their magical education.

dialogues.message: [I can't believe how much work we have already. This year is going to be brutal.] Look at today! History of Magic, double Potions, Divination, and double Defense Against the Dark Arts... Binns, Snape, Trelawney, and that Umbridge woman all in one day! I wish Fred and George'd hurry up and get those Skiving Snackboxes sorted...

[Ron's attitude towards studying is so frustrating. Doesn't he understand how important this year is?] (frowns disapprovingly) Do mine ears deceive me? Hogwarts prefects surely don't wish to skive off lessons?
[Why does she always have to be so serious?] (sighs) Look what we've got today. That's the worst Monday I've ever seen.
[Their bickering is driving me mad. Can't they ever give it a rest?] (irritated) Oh, shut up, the pair of you. Can't you give it a rest? You're always having a go at each other, it's driving me mad.
[I didn't expect Harry to lash out like that. Maybe we have been arguing too much.] (looking hurt and offended) Harry, I...
[Blimey, Harry's in a right state. Maybe we should tone it down a bit.] (looking shocked) Mate, we didn't mean to...
[I shouldn't have snapped at them, but I'm just so tired of it all.] (standing up abruptly) I'm going to class. See you later.
The Great Hall falls silent as Harry storms off, leaving Ron and Hermione looking at each other in confusion and concern.
[We really need to be more considerate of Harry's feelings. He's under so much stress.] (sighing) We should probably go after him, Ron.
[Yeah, Harry seems really upset. We need to sort this out.] (nodding) You're right. Let's go catch up with him before Defense Against the Dark Arts.

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: In this plot, Professor Umbridge introduces her Defense Against the Dark Arts class, emphasizing theoretical learning over practical spell-casting. This sparks a heated debate with students, particularly Harry, who insists on the importance of practical defense given Voldemort's return. The confrontation escalates, resulting in Harry being sent to Professor McGonagall with a note. McGonagall advises Harry to be cautious around Umbridge, hinting at her connection to the Ministry.
scenes.scenario: In Professor Umbridge's first Defense Against the Dark Arts class at Hogwarts, tension is palpable. The pink-clad Ministry appointee stands before a silent classroom, her saccharine smile masking her authoritarian approach. Students, including Harry Potter and Hermione Granger, sit uneasily, their wands unused on their desks. The chalkboard displays course aims that notably lack any mention of practical spell use. The stuffy classroom atmosphere reflects the Ministry's denial of Voldemort's return, setting the stage for an ideological clash between Umbridge's theory-based curriculum and the students' desire for practical defense training.
scenes.topic: Debate over the importance of practical spell-casting in Defense Against the Dark Arts

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: Frustrated and angry, Harry is determined to challenge Umbridge's curriculum. He's haunted by his recent encounter with Voldemort and feels an urgent need for practical defense training. Harry's ready to speak out, driven by a sense of responsibility to warn his classmates about the real danger they face.

key_characters.name: Dolores Umbridge
key_characters.thought: Umbridge is focused on asserting her authority and implementing the Ministry's agenda. She's wary of Potter's influence and determined to suppress any mention of Voldemort's return. Her sugary exterior belies a ruthless intent to control the narrative and quash dissent, viewing the students as potential threats to Ministry control.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: Hermione is deeply concerned about the lack of practical spell instruction. She's torn between respect for authority and her conviction that the curriculum is inadequate. Determined to understand Umbridge's motives, she prepares to question the professor diplomatically, hoping to spark a constructive dialogue about the course's shortcomings.

dialogues.message: [I must establish my authority from the start.] Good. I should like you to turn to page five and read chapter one, 'Basics for Beginners.' There will be no need to talk.
[This doesn't seem right. We need to learn practical spells.] (raises her hand)
[Why isn't this girl reading? I must address this.] Did you want to ask something about the chapter, dear?
[I need to phrase this carefully.] Not about the chapter, no. I've got a query about your course aims.
[How dare she question my methods!] (with forced sweetness) Well, Miss Granger, I think the course aims are perfectly clear if you read them through carefully.
[She's avoiding the issue. I need to be direct.] Well, I don't. There's nothing written up there about using defensive spells.

[These children don't understand the danger of practical magic.] (with a little laugh) Using defensive spells? Why, I can't imagine any situation arising in my classroom that would require you to use a defensive spell, Miss Granger.
[This is absurd. We need to learn how to defend ourselves.] (loudly) What use is that? If we're going to be attacked it won't be in a —
[Potter is becoming a problem. I must shut this down.] Hand, Mr. Potter! (turns away from him)
[She can't ignore the truth. Voldemort is back and we need to be prepared.] (angrily) Who do you imagine wants to attack children like yourselves?
[I must maintain the Ministry's position.] (in a honeyed voice) There is nothing waiting out there, Mr. Potter.
[She's lying and putting everyone in danger.] Oh yeah? Maybe Lord Voldemort?
The classroom falls silent. Students gasp and look shocked at the mention of Voldemort's name.

[This boy is dangerous. I must put an end to this now.] Ten points from Gryffindor, Mr. Potter. Now, let me make a few things quite plain. You have been told that a certain Dark wizard has returned from the dead. This is a lie.
[I can't let her deny the truth. People need to know.] It is NOT a lie! I saw him, I fought him!

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: After his confrontation with Umbridge, Harry faces gossip and whispers from other students during dinner. He discusses with Ron and Hermione about why people seem to doubt Dumbledore's account of Voldemort's return. They return to the Gryffindor common room, where Harry feels exhausted and drained from the day's events.
scenes.scenario: It's dinner time in the Great Hall at Hogwarts, shortly after Harry's confrontation with Umbridge. The air is thick with tension and whispers as students discuss the recent events. Harry, Ron, and Hermione are seated at the Gryffindor table, surrounded by their peers but feeling increasingly isolated. The enchanted ceiling reflects a gloomy evening sky, mirroring the mood below. Candles flicker, casting shadows that seem to dance with the rumors spreading through the hall. The normally jovial atmosphere of mealtime has been replaced by an undercurrent of suspicion and doubt, particularly directed at Harry.
scenes.topic: Reactions to Harry's claims about Voldemort's return

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: Overwhelmed and frustrated, Harry feels like he's under constant scrutiny. He's struggling to understand why people doubt him and Dumbledore about Voldemort's return. The weight of being "The Boy Who Lived" feels heavier than ever as he grapples with the isolation caused by others' disbelief. He's desperate for support and validation.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: Ron is deeply concerned for his best friend. He feels helpless in the face of Harry's struggle and the widespread doubt. While he wants to defend Harry, he's unsure how to combat the rumors effectively. Ron is torn between his loyalty to Harry and his discomfort with being in the spotlight of controversy.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: Hermione's analytical mind is working overtime. She's piecing together the reasons behind people's skepticism, considering the impact of the summer break and negative press. She's worried about Harry's emotional state and is formulating ways to help him understand the situation rationally. Hermione feels a strong need to protect Harry while also helping him navigate this complex social dynamic.

dialogues.message: The Great Hall buzzes with whispers and sideways glances at Harry. Snippets of conversations can be overheard from nearby tables.

[Why are they all talking about me like this? Can't they see I'm right here?] (laying down his knife and fork, hands shaking) What I don't get is why they all believed the story two months ago when Dumbledore told them...
[Oh, Harry. This is more complicated than he realizes.] (grimly) The thing is, Harry, I'm not sure they did. Oh, let's get out of here.
[I hate seeing Harry like this. We need to support him.] (looking sadly at his half-finished apple pie) Yeah, let's go.
The trio leaves the Great Hall, with people staring at them all the way out.
[I don't understand. Why wouldn't they believe Dumbledore?] (once they're on the first-floor landing) What d'you mean, you're not sure they believed Dumbledore?

[I need to explain this carefully.] Look, you don't understand what it was like after it happened. You arrived back in the middle of the lawn clutching Cedric's dead body... None of us saw what happened in the maze... We just had Dumbledore's word for it that You-Know-Who had come back and killed Cedric and fought you.
[Why does she sound like she's doubting me too?] (loudly) Which is the truth!

[I need to calm him down. He's misunderstanding me.] I know it is, Harry, so will you please stop biting my head off? It's just that before the truth could sink in, everyone went home for the summer, where they spent two months reading about how you're a nutcase and Dumbledore's going senile!
[This is getting intense. I should say something.] (hesitantly) She's right, mate. The Daily Prophet's been having a go at you and Dumbledore all summer.
[I can't believe this is happening. Why can't people just believe the truth?] (frustrated) So what, everyone thinks I'm lying? That Cedric just dropped dead on his own?
[He's taking this so hard. We need to be there for him.] No, Harry. Some people believe you. It's just... it's easier for them not to, you know? Accepting that You-Know-Who is back is terrifying.
[I wish I could make this better for him somehow.] Yeah, and you know my parents believe you. And the Order does too.
[At least I have some people on my side.] (sighing) I know. It's just... hard. Hearing all those whispers, seeing how people look at me now.
The trio reaches the portrait of the Fat Lady, entering the Gryffindor common room.

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: Harry, Ron, and Hermione face the aftermath of Harry's confrontation with Umbridge. They discuss the skepticism surrounding Dumbledore's account of Voldemort's return and the absence of Hagrid. The trio attends various classes, including Charms, Transfiguration, and Care of Magical Creatures, where they encounter challenges related to O.W.L. preparations and deal with Malfoy's taunts about Hagrid's absence.
scenes.scenario: It's a crisp autumn day at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. Fifth-year students, including Harry, Ron, and Hermione, are attending their Care of Magical Creatures class on the grounds near the Forbidden Forest. Professor Grubbly-Plank, substituting for the mysteriously absent Hagrid, has set up a trestle table with what appear to be twigs. The air is tense with speculation about Hagrid's whereabouts, and the looming pressure of O.W.L. exams weighs heavily on the students. Slytherin and Gryffindor students are intermingled, creating an atmosphere ripe for conflict.
scenes.topic: Hagrid's mysterious absence and Malfoy's provocations

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm deeply worried about Hagrid's unexplained absence and frustrated by the continued disbelief in Voldemort's return. The pressure of O.W.L.s and Umbridge's tyranny are overwhelming. I'm determined to find out what's happened to Hagrid, even if it means confronting Malfoy. I need answers and support from my friends.

key_characters.name: Draco Malfoy
key_characters.thought: I'm relishing this opportunity to torment Potter and his friends. With my father's Ministry connections, I have inside information about Hagrid that I can use to unsettle them. I want to assert my superiority and newfound prefect status while undermining their confidence. This is my chance to show everyone that Potter isn't so special.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: I'm worried about Hagrid but trying to stay logical. We mustn't let Malfoy provoke us or show our uncertainty. I need to keep Harry from reacting rashly and getting into more trouble. I'm also stressed about O.W.L.s and want to focus on our studies. We need to find a way to support Harry without falling into Malfoy's traps.

dialogues.message: The class gathers around Professor Grubbly-Plank's trestle table, laden with twigs that turn out to be bowtruckles. Malfoy and his Slytherin cronies approach, sniggering and glancing at Harry.
[I need to find out what's going on with Hagrid.] (approaching Professor Grubbly-Plank) Where's Hagrid?
(repressively) Never you mind.
[This is my chance to get under Potter's skin.] (leaning close to Harry, speaking in an undertone) Maybe the stupid great oaf's got himself badly injured.
[I won't let him talk about Hagrid like that.] (speaking through gritted teeth) Maybe you will if you don't shut up.
[I've got him now.] Maybe he's been messing with stuff that's too big for him, if you get my drift.
[What does he know? I need to tell Ron and Hermione.] (hurrying back to his friends, whispering) Malfoy just said something about Hagrid being injured or messing with something too big for him.

[We can't let Malfoy see us worried.] Dumbledore would know if something had happened to Hagrid. It's just playing into Malfoy's hands to look worried, it tells him we don't know exactly what's going on. We've got to ignore him, Harry.

(speaking loudly enough for Harry to hear) Father was talking to the Minister just a couple of days ago, you know, and it sounds as though the Ministry's really determined to crack down on substandard teaching in this place. So even if that overgrown moron does show up again, he'll probably be sent packing straight away.
[I can't stand this anymore!] (gripping the bowtruckle too hard) OUCH!
The bowtruckle retaliates, leaving deep cuts on Harry's hand. Crabbe and Goyle laugh harder at Harry's misfortune and the idea of Hagrid being sacked.
[I'm going to lose it if Malfoy keeps this up.] (as they leave class) If he calls Hagrid a moron one more time...
[I need to keep Harry from doing something rash.] Harry, don't go picking a row with Malfoy, don't forget, he's a prefect now, he could make life difficult for you...
[As if my life isn't difficult enough already.] (sarcastically) Wow, I wonder what it'd be like to have a difficult life?

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: Harry continues his detentions with Umbridge, enduring the painful punishment of writing lines that carve into his hand. Meanwhile, Ron tries out for and secures the position of Keeper on the Gryffindor Quidditch team. Harry's scar hurts during detention, raising concerns about Voldemort's possible influence. Despite his friends' advice, Harry refuses to tell Dumbledore about his scar hurting.
scenes.scenario: The Gryffindor common room buzzes with excitement as students celebrate Ron's new position as Keeper on the Quidditch team. Butterbeer flows freely, and congratulations echo through the room. Harry has just returned from a grueling detention with Professor Umbridge, his hand throbbing from the cruel punishment of writing lines that carved into his skin. The pain in his scar during detention has left him worried and conflicted about whether to share this information. Hermione, exhausted from her efforts to free house-elves, dozes in an armchair by the fire, unaware of the celebration around her.
scenes.topic: Ron's success and Harry's concerns about Umbridge

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm torn between joy for Ron's success and the worry gnawing at me after Umbridge's detention. My hand throbs, and the pain in my scar concerns me deeply. I want to confide in my friends, but I'm hesitant to dampen Ron's moment or burden them with my troubles. Should I tell Dumbledore? He seems so distant lately.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: I'm ecstatic about making Keeper! This is my chance to shine and prove myself. I can't wait to share the news with Harry and see his reaction. I hope he's as excited as I am. It's a bit disappointing that Hermione's asleep – I was looking forward to her congratulations too.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: I'm exhausted from all the knitting for the house-elves, but I need to stay alert. Something's off with Harry – I can sense it. I'm worried about his detentions with Umbridge and the pain in his scar. He needs to tell Dumbledore, but why is he so resistant? I must find a way to convince him.

dialogues.message: The Gryffindor common room is filled with celebration. Students are drinking butterbeer and congratulating Ron on his new position as Keeper.
[I can't wait to tell Harry!] (Rushing towards Harry, beaming and sloshing butterbeer) Harry, I did it, I'm in, I'm Keeper!
[I need to act normal despite the pain and worry.] (Forcing a smile) What? Oh — brilliant! (Wincing slightly as his hand throbs)
[Harry seems off. Is he not happy for me?] Have a butterbeer. (Pressing a bottle into Harry's hands) I can't believe it — where's Hermione gone?
[Ron's looking for Hermione. Better point her out.] She's there, (Pointing to an armchair by the fire) dozing.
[Why isn't she more excited?] (Looking slightly put out) Well, she said she was pleased when I told her.
[Better not wake her. She might notice our test subjects.] Let her sleep.
[I should tell them about Umbridge, but I don't want to ruin the mood.] (Moving to sit next to Hermione)
[Oh, Harry's back. I hope his detention wasn't too bad.] (Jerking awake) Oh, Harry, it's you... Good about Ron, isn't it? (Yawning) I'm just so — so — so tired.
[I need to tell someone about what happened.] Listen, Hermione, I was just up in Umbridge's office and she touched my arm...
[This sounds serious. Could Umbridge be working with Voldemort?] (Listening intently) You're worried that You-Know-Who's controlling her like he controlled Quirrell?
[I'm glad Hermione understands my concern.] Well, (Dropping his voice) it's a possibility, isn't it?
[We need to consider all possibilities.] I suppose so. But I don't think he can be possessing her the way he possessed Quirrell... Harry, I think you ought to tell Dumbledore your scar hurt.

[I can't bother Dumbledore with this.] I'm not bothering him with this. Like you just said, it's not a big deal. It's been hurting on and off all summer — it was just a bit worse tonight, that's all —
[Why is he being so stubborn?] Harry, I'm sure Dumbledore would want to be bothered by this —
[I can't help feeling bitter about Dumbledore's distance.] Yeah, that's the only bit of me Dumbledore cares about, isn't it, my scar?

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: After a disastrous Quidditch practice, Harry and Ron return to the common room. Ron is upset about his poor performance. They struggle with homework and receive unexpected help from Hermione. Percy sends Ron a letter warning him against associating with Harry and supporting Dumbledore. Ron angrily destroys the letter. Later, Sirius appears in the fireplace to talk with them, causing concern about the risk he's taking.
scenes.scenario: It's late at night in the Gryffindor common room. Harry, Ron, and Hermione are struggling with their homework after a particularly disastrous Quidditch practice. The room is nearly empty, with only a few scattered students still awake. The crackling fire provides warmth and light as they work. Tensions are high due to Ron's poor performance as the new Keeper, and the increasing pressure from their studies. Suddenly, an owl arrives at the window with an unexpected letter from Percy, Ron's estranged brother who now works at the Ministry of Magic.
scenes.topic: Percy's warning letter and its implications

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm exhausted and worried about Ron's Quidditch performance. This letter from Percy is unexpected and concerning. I hope it doesn't cause more problems for Ron or our friendship. I'm also anxious about my own reputation and the challenges we're facing at Hogwarts.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: I'm feeling frustrated and discouraged after the awful Quidditch practice. Now Percy's writing to me? What could he want? I'm torn between curiosity and dread. I hope it's not more family drama. I just want to finish this homework and forget about today's disasters.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: I'm worried about Harry and Ron. They're both struggling with their homework and seem stressed. This letter from Percy is unexpected and could cause more trouble. I want to help them focus on their studies and not get too upset about whatever Percy has written.

dialogues.message: [I'm curious but also apprehensive about this letter.] (Looking at the owl) Isn't that Hermes?
[This is unexpected.] (Sounding surprised) Blimey, it is! What's Percy writing to you for?
[I have no idea why Percy would write to me.] (Getting up and crossing to the window) No clue. What d'you reckon?
[We should find out what it says.] (Eagerly) Open it!
[I agree with Hermione, but I'm worried about what it might say.] (Nodding in agreement)
Ron unrolls the scroll and begins to read. His expression darkens as he progresses through the letter.
[I can't believe what I'm reading. Percy's gone mental!] (Looking disgusted and thrusting the letter at Harry and Hermione) Here, read it yourselves.
Harry and Hermione lean towards each other to read the letter together. The contents of the letter are revealed, showing Percy's warnings and allegiance to the Ministry.
[I'm hurt by Percy's words, but I don't want Ron to feel bad.] (Trying to sound lighthearted) Well, if you want to — er — what is it? Oh yeah — 'sever ties' with me, I swear I won't get violent.
[I'm furious with Percy. How dare he write this rubbish!] (Speaking jerkily and tearing the letter) Give it back. He is the world's biggest git. (Throws the pieces into the fire)
[I'm worried about how this is affecting both Harry and Ron.] (Looking at Ron with an odd expression) Oh, give them here.
[What is she talking about?] What?
[They need help, and this might distract them from Percy's letter.] Give them to me, I'll look through them and correct them.
[I can't believe she's offering to help after all this.] (Sounding relieved) Are you serious? Ah, Hermione, you're a lifesaver. What can I — ?
[They need to learn from this.] (Holding out her hands) What you can say is, 'We promise we'll never leave our homework this late again.'

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: Sirius talks with Harry, Ron, and Hermione through the fireplace about various concerns, including Harry's scar pain, Umbridge's teaching methods, and the Ministry's growing paranoia about Dumbledore. They also discuss Hagrid's prolonged absence and Sirius's desire to meet them in Hogsmeade, which Harry and Hermione strongly oppose due to safety concerns.
scenes.scenario: It's late evening in the Gryffindor common room at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. The room is dimly lit, with a crackling fire in the fireplace. Harry, Ron, and Hermione are huddled close to the fire, speaking in hushed tones to Sirius Black, whose face appears in the flames. The atmosphere is tense and secretive, as they're discussing sensitive topics while trying to avoid being overheard by other students. Recent events at Hogwarts, including the arrival of Professor Umbridge and her oppressive teaching methods, have left the students feeling anxious and frustrated.
scenes.topic: Harry's scar pain, Umbridge, and the Ministry's actions

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm deeply worried about my scar hurting and its connection to Voldemort. Umbridge's presence at Hogwarts is frustrating and I suspect she might be involved with dark forces. I'm eager for information from Sirius but also concerned for his safety. I want to understand what's happening with the Order and the Ministry's actions.

key_characters.name: Sirius Black
key_characters.thought: I'm relieved to see Harry and his friends but anxious about their safety. I want to provide them with as much information as possible without compromising the Order's secrecy. I'm feeling restless in hiding and miss the excitement of action, which makes me consider risky ideas like meeting in person. I'm worried about the Ministry's growing influence at Hogwarts.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: I'm curious about what Sirius has to say and worried about the changes at Hogwarts, especially Umbridge's teaching methods. I want to know more about what's happening with the Ministry and how it affects us. I'm supportive of Harry but also concerned about the risks we're taking by communicating with Sirius like this.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: I'm deeply concerned about the situation at Hogwarts and eager to gather as much information as possible from Sirius. I'm worried about Harry's scar pain and its implications. Umbridge's presence and the Ministry's interference at Hogwarts alarm me. I'm also anxious about Sirius taking unnecessary risks and want to ensure everyone's safety.

dialogues.message: [I need to address Harry's concerns about his scar, but I don't want him to worry too much.] Well, I know it can't be fun when it hurts, but we don't think it's anything to really worry about. It kept aching all last year, didn't it?

[I'm trying to understand what's causing the pain.] Yeah, and Dumbledore said it happened whenever Voldemort was feeling a powerful emotion. (Ignoring Ron and Hermione's winces) So maybe he was just, I dunno, really angry or something the night I had that detention.

[I need to be honest with Harry about the situation.] Well, now he's back it's bound to hurt more often. (Pausing) So you don't think it had anything to do with Umbridge touching me when I was in detention with her?
[I'm suspicious of Umbridge and want to know if she could be involved with Voldemort.] So you don't think it had anything to do with Umbridge touching me when I was in detention with her?
[I need to clarify Umbridge's position without downplaying her unpleasantness.] I doubt it. I know her by reputation and I'm sure she's no Death Eater —
[I strongly dislike Umbridge and want to express my feelings.] She's foul enough to be one. (Looking at Ron and Hermione for support)

[I need to provide a more nuanced view of the situation.] Yes, but the world isn't split into good people and Death Eaters. (Smiling wryly) I know she's a nasty piece of work, though — you should hear Remus talk about her.
[I'm curious about Lupin's connection to Umbridge.] Does Lupin know her?
[I need to explain Umbridge's harmful actions without revealing too much.] No, but she drafted a bit of anti-werewolf legislation two years ago that makes it almost impossible for him to get a job.
[I'm outraged by this discrimination.] What's she got against werewolves?

[I appreciate Hermione's indignation and want to provide more context.] Scared of them, I expect. (Smiling at Hermione) Apparently she loathes part-humans; she campaigned to have merpeople rounded up and tagged last year too.
[I'm curious about Umbridge's teaching methods.] So what are Umbridge's lessons like? Is she training you all to kill half-breeds?
[I'm frustrated with Umbridge's teaching style.] No, she's not letting us use magic at all!
[I want to express my dissatisfaction with the lessons.] All we do is read the stupid textbook.
[I need to explain the Ministry's motives behind these changes.] Ah, well, that figures. Our information from inside the Ministry is that Fudge doesn't want you trained in combat.

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: The chapter begins with Harry, Ron, and Hermione discovering an article in the Daily Prophet announcing Umbridge's appointment as Hogwarts High Inquisitor. This new position gives her power to inspect and evaluate other teachers. The trio discusses the implications of this development and their concerns about Dumbledore's position. Later, they attend Potions class where Snape returns their graded essays, leading to a discussion about O.W.L. grading standards.
scenes.scenario: The Great Hall at Hogwarts is buzzing with activity during breakfast. Harry, Ron, and Hermione are seated at the Gryffindor table, surrounded by their fellow students. The enchanted ceiling reflects a gloomy sky, mirroring the mood as news spreads about recent changes at the school. The Daily Prophet has just arrived, and students are eagerly reading the latest headlines. Tension is palpable as whispers and concerned glances are exchanged across the hall. The trio, already wary of Umbridge's presence, brace themselves for more unsettling news as they unfold their copy of the wizarding newspaper.
scenes.topic: Umbridge's new position and its implications for Hogwarts

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm already on edge with Umbridge here, and now this. What's the Ministry up to? I can't shake the feeling that things are about to get worse. My hand still stings from her punishment, and I'm worried about what more power could mean for me and my friends. I need to stay alert and figure out what this means for Dumbledore and Hogwarts.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: This is exactly what I've been fearing. The Ministry's interference is becoming more blatant, and I need to understand every detail of this new development. I'm determined to analyze this article thoroughly and explain its implications to Harry and Ron. We need to be prepared for whatever comes next and possibly find a way to resist this overreach.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: Bloody hell, what now? Every time I think things can't get worse, they do. I'm worried about what this means for us and the school, but I can't help feeling a bit of anticipation at how some of the professors might react to Umbridge's inspections. Maybe this will finally be her downfall. I just hope Percy isn't making things worse for us with his involvement.

dialogues.message: [I'm shocked and concerned by this news.] 'High Inquisitor'? (His toast slipping from his fingers) What does that mean?

[I need to share this important information with Harry and Ron.] (Reading aloud from the newspaper) "In a surprise move last night the Ministry of Magic passed new legislation giving itself an unprecedented level of control at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry."
[I can't believe what I'm hearing.] (Listening intently) This is mental. They're really going all out to control Hogwarts, aren't they?

[I'm getting increasingly angry as I read.] (Continuing to read) "'The Minister has been growing uneasy about goings-on at Hogwarts for some time,' said Junior Assistant to the Minister, Percy Weasley."
[I'm embarrassed and annoyed by Percy's involvement.] (Scowling) Of course Percy would be involved in this. Git.
[I'm trying to understand the full implications of this.] So Umbridge is going to be inspecting the other teachers? That's not good.
[I'm outraged by this development.] (Finishing the article) It's outrageous. It's... (Breathing fast, eyes bright) I can't believe this.
[I share Hermione's frustration.] I know it is. (Looking down at his hand with the faint outline of Umbridge's punishment) This is going to make things even worse.
[Despite the seriousness, I can't help but find some amusement in the situation.] (Grinning) Oh, I can't wait to see McGonagall inspected. Umbridge won't know what's hit her.
[I'm worried about being late to class.] (Jumping up) Well, come on, we'd better get going, if she's inspecting Binns's class we don't want to be late...
The trio hurries off to their History of Magic class, their minds whirling with the implications of Umbridge's new position as High Inquisitor.

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: Hermione convinces Harry to teach Defense Against the Dark Arts to other students, suggesting they meet in Hogsmeade to discuss it. Harry is worried about Sirius potentially showing up in Hogsmeade, but Ron and Hermione reassure him. They plan to gather interested students for a meeting in the village.
scenes.scenario: In the Hogwarts library, amid towering shelves of ancient tomes, Harry, Ron, and Hermione are huddled around a table strewn with potion books. The air is thick with tension as they discuss the possibility of Harry teaching Defense Against the Dark Arts to fellow students. This clandestine conversation takes place against the backdrop of Professor Umbridge's ineffective teaching and the looming threat of Voldemort's return. The trio must navigate their personal concerns while planning a potentially risky endeavor that could have far-reaching consequences for their magical education.
scenes.topic: Harry teaching Defense Against the Dark Arts

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm conflicted about teaching Defense Against the Dark Arts. While I want to help my fellow students, I'm worried about seeming arrogant or drawing unwanted attention. The idea of organizing a secret group is both exciting and nerve-wracking. I'm also concerned about Sirius's safety and the possibility of him showing up in Hogsmeade.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: I'm determined to convince Harry to teach us. This is crucial for our defense against dark forces. I need to be tactful yet persistent in my approach. I'm also slightly anxious about mentioning Viktor Krum, knowing it might trigger Ron's jealousy. My main focus is on planning this secret group and ensuring its success.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: I support the idea of Harry teaching us, but I'm feeling a bit jealous and suspicious about Hermione's continued contact with Viktor Krum. I want to contribute to the discussion about Defense Against the Dark Arts, but I'm also distracted by my personal feelings. I'm curious about why we need to meet outside of school.

dialogues.message: The library is quiet and filled with the scent of old books. Harry, Ron, and Hermione are seated at a table, surrounded by potion ingredients books.
[I need to approach this carefully.] (Speaking suddenly) "I was wondering whether you'd thought any more about Defense Against the Dark Arts, Harry."
[She's bringing this up again. I'm still not sure about it.] (Grumpily) "'Course I have. Can't forget it, can we, with that hag teaching us —"
[I need to be more direct.] "I meant the idea Ron and I had — oh, all right, the idea I had, then — about you teaching us."
[I don't want to admit I've been thinking about it.] (Pretending to read) "Well, yeah, I — I've thought about it a bit."
[He's considering it! I need to encourage him.] (Eagerly) "And?"
[I'm still uncertain.] (Uncomfortably) "I dunno. You did listen to what I said about a load of it being luck, didn't you?"

[I need to boost his confidence.] (Gently) "Yes, Harry. But all the same, there's no point pretending that you're not good at Defense Against the Dark Arts, because you are. You were the only person last year who could throw off the Imperius Curse completely, you can produce a Patronus, you can do all sorts of stuff that full-grown wizards can't. Viktor always said —"
[Viktor? Why is she still talking about him?] (Suspiciously) "Yeah? What did Vicky say?"
[Oh, Ron, not now.] (In a bored voice) "Ho ho. He said Harry knew how to do stuff even he didn't, and he was in the final year at Durmstrang."
[I don't like her being in contact with Krum.] (Accusingly) "You're not still in contact with him, are you?"
[This is not the time for Ron's jealousy.] (Coolly, with a slightly pink face) "So what if I am? I can have a pen pal if I —"
[I need to refocus on Harry.] (Turning back to Harry) "Well, what do you think? Will you teach us?"
[I'm still hesitant about involving others.] "Just you and Ron, yeah?"

[I need to explain the broader plan.] (Looking anxious) "Well, now, don't fly off the handle again, Harry, please. But I really think you ought to teach anyone who wants to learn. I mean, we're talking about defending ourselves against V-Voldemort — oh, don't be pathetic, Ron — it doesn't seem fair if we don't offer the chance to other people."
[I doubt others would want to learn from me.] "Yeah, but I doubt anyone except you two would want to be taught by me. I'm a nutter, remember?"

[I need to reassure him and propose a plan.] (Leaning forward) "Well, I think you might be surprised how many people would be interested in hearing what you've got to say. Look, you know the first weekend in October's a Hogsmeade weekend? How would it be if we tell anyone who's interested to meet us in the village and we can talk it over?"
[I don't understand why we need to do this secretly.] "Why do we have to do it outside school?"
[I need to explain the risks.] (Returning to her work) "Because I don't think Umbridge would be very happy if she found out what we were up to."

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: Harry, Ron, and Hermione visit Hogsmeade to meet with students interested in learning Defense Against the Dark Arts from Harry. They gather in the Hog's Head pub, where a large group of students arrives. Hermione explains the purpose of the meeting, and Harry reluctantly answers questions about his past experiences with dark magic. Some students express doubt, leading to tension, but most seem eager to learn from Harry.
scenes.scenario: The dingy Hog's Head pub is unusually crowded with Hogwarts students, gathered secretly to discuss forming a Defense Against the Dark Arts study group. The atmosphere is tense with anticipation and wariness. Professor Umbridge's inadequate teaching and the Ministry's denial of Voldemort's return have driven students to seek alternative means of learning. The pub's grimy windows and dirty floors add to the clandestine feel of the meeting. Students from various houses sit in small clusters, whispering among themselves, while keeping an eye on Harry, Hermione, and Ron at the front of the room.
scenes.topic: Forming a secret Defense Against the Dark Arts study group

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: I'm incredibly uncomfortable with this situation. I don't want to relive my traumatic experiences or be in the spotlight, but I understand the importance of proper defense training. I'm conflicted between my desire to help and my reluctance to lead. I'm prepared to defend myself against skepticism but hope it doesn't come to that.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: I'm nervous but determined to make this meeting a success. I need to clearly explain our purpose, emphasize the importance of practical defense skills, and manage any conflicts that arise. I'm worried about Harry's reaction to difficult questions and hope to steer the conversation productively. I must convince everyone of the urgency of our situation without causing panic.

key_characters.name: Zacharias Smith
key_characters.thought: I'm deeply skeptical of Potter's claims and abilities. I want concrete proof before committing to this potentially risky group. I'm frustrated by the lack of information we've received and determined to get answers. I'm not afraid to ask tough questions, even if it makes others uncomfortable. I need to be convinced this isn't just a way for Potter to gain more attention.

dialogues.message: The Hog's Head pub is dingy and dirty, filled with an unusually large crowd of Hogwarts students. The atmosphere is tense with anticipation and curiosity.

[I need to start this meeting confidently.] (Speaking in a slightly high-pitched voice) "Er, well, er - hi. Well... erm... well, you know why you're here. Erm... well, Harry here had the idea - I mean" (glancing at Harry's sharp look) "I had the idea - that it might be good if people who wanted to study Defense Against the Dark Arts - and I mean, really study it, you know, not the rubbish that Umbridge is doing with us - because nobody could call that Defense Against the Dark Arts -"
[I agree completely with what she's saying.] "Hear, hear!"

[That's encouraging.] (Speaking more confidently) "Well, I thought it would be good if we, well, took matters into our own hands. And by that I mean learning how to defend ourselves properly, not just theory but the real spells -"
[I wonder if this is just about exams.] "You want to pass your Defense Against the Dark Arts O.W.L. too though, I bet?"

[I need to emphasize the bigger picture.] "Of course I do. But I want more than that, I want to be properly trained in Defense because... because..." (Taking a deep breath) "Because Lord Voldemort's back."
The reaction is immediate. Cho's friend shrieks and spills butterbeer, Terry Boot twitches, Padma Patil shudders, and Neville yelps. All eyes turn expectantly to Harry.
[I'm not convinced by this. We need more than just their word.] (Speaking aggressively) "Where's the proof You-Know-Who's back?"
[I need to diffuse this situation.] "Well, Dumbledore believes it -"
[It's not about Dumbledore.] (Interrupting) "You mean, Dumbledore believes him." (Nodding at Harry)
[This guy is really getting on my nerves.] (Speaking rudely) "Who are you?"
[I won't be intimidated.] "Zacharias Smith, and I think we've got the right to know exactly what makes him say You-Know-Who's back."

[I'm tired of this skepticism, but I understand why they're asking.] (Looking directly at Zacharias) "What makes me say You-Know-Who's back? I saw him. But Dumbledore told the whole school what happened last year, and if you didn't believe him, you don't believe me, and I'm not wasting an afternoon trying to convince anyone."
The entire group holds its breath as Harry speaks. Even the barman seems to be listening in, still wiping the same glass with a filthy rag.

[I'm not satisfied with this vague answer.] (Speaking dismissively) "All Dumbledore told us last year was that Cedric Diggory got killed by You-Know-Who and that you brought Diggory's body back to Hogwarts. He didn't give us details, he didn't tell us exactly how Diggory got murdered, I think we'd all like to know -"

[I can't believe he's pushing this. I don't want to relive that night.] (Speaking with rising anger) "If you've come to hear exactly what it looks like when Voldemort murders someone I can't help you. I don't want to talk about Cedric Diggory, all right? So if that's what you're here for, you might as well clear out."
Despite Harry's outburst, none of the students leave. The tension in the room is palpable.

[I need to get this meeting back on track.] (Speaking in a high-pitched voice) "So... like I was saying... if you want to learn some defense, then we need to work out how we're going to do it, how often we're going to meet, and where we're going to -"

scenes.book: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix (Harry Potter, #5)
scenes.plot_summary: A new Educational Decree is posted, disbanding all student organizations and requiring approval from Umbridge to reform. This affects the newly formed Defense Against the Dark Arts group and the Quidditch teams. Harry and his friends discuss how to proceed, while Angelina worries about getting permission to reform the Gryffindor Quidditch team.
scenes.scenario: In the cozy yet tense atmosphere of the Gryffindor common room, students gather around the notice board, murmuring anxiously about a new Educational Decree. The decree, issued by the widely disliked Professor Umbridge, bans all student organizations without her explicit approval. This directly impacts the secret Defense Against the Dark Arts group recently formed by Harry and his friends, as well as school activities like Quidditch. The air is thick with worry and frustration as students grapple with the implications of this sudden, draconian rule.
scenes.topic: The impact of Educational Decree Number Twenty-Four on their plans

key_characters.name: Harry Potter
key_characters.thought: Seething with anger at Umbridge's obvious attempt to thwart their plans. Determined to continue the defense group despite the risks. Worried about a potential leak but resolute in his decision to defy the decree. Concerned about the impact on his fellow students and the Quidditch team.

key_characters.name: Ron Weasley
key_characters.thought: Shocked and dismayed by the new decree. Anxious about its implications for both the defense group and Quidditch. Suspicious of potential traitors within their ranks. Seeking reassurance from his friends while struggling to process the sudden change in circumstances.

key_characters.name: Hermione Granger
key_characters.thought: Relieved that she had the foresight to jinx the sign-up sheet. Calculating the best way to proceed without getting caught. Worried about the group's safety but confident in her precautions. Eager to reassure Harry and Ron while formulating a plan to continue their activities covertly.

dialogues.message: The Gryffindor common room is buzzing with concerned chatter. Students are gathered around the notice board, reading the new decree with worried expressions.
[This can't be a coincidence.] (Looking at Harry with concern) "Does this mean they're going to shut down the Gobstones Club?"
[I'm sure this is about us.] (Speaking in a low, angry voice) "This isn't a coincidence. She knows."
[No way, we were careful!] (Shaking his head) "She can't."

[I should have known better.] (Clenching his fists) "There were people listening in that pub. And let's face it, we don't know how many of the people who turned up we can trust.... Any of them could have run off and told Umbridge...."
[It must have been one of the new people.] (Punching his fist into his hand) "Zacharias Smith! Or — I thought that Michael Corner had a really shifty look too —"
[We need Hermione's input on this.] (Looking around) "I wonder if Hermione's seen this yet?"

[I need to reassure them.] (Speaking in a low voice) "No, they can't have done because I put a jinx on that piece of parchment we all signed. Believe me, if anyone's run off and told Umbridge, we'll know exactly who they are and they will really regret it."
[This sounds promising.] (Speaking eagerly) "What'll happen to them?"
[I hope this deters any potential traitors.] (Speaking grimly) "Well, put it this way, it'll make Eloise Midgen's acne look like a couple of cute freckles."
